items.name: TradeZoro GEX Levels
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Call wall, put wall, zero gamma, IV ±68% and market levels (pVAH/pPOC/pVAL, ONH/ONL) from the GEX page (SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, NQ and gold GC)
items.summary: Draws the call wall, put wall, zero gamma, the IV 68% range and prior-session levels from the GEX page as lines on your chart.
overview: TradeZoro GEX Levels puts the lines from the GEX page on your chart, with the same names, colours and line styles. By default you see the call wall, the zero gamma (flip) line, the put wall, the IV +68% and -68% range, and the market levels pVAH, pPOC, pVAL, ONH and ONL.

Optional extras include the 0DTE call and put walls, a gamma profile drawn as bars by strike, a shaded 68% band, the next three biggest strikes, ranked strikes with a role tag, the IV 80% range, and RTH session levels. Labels that sit within a few pixels of each other merge into one tag, and a note at the bottom shows when the data was last updated (for example 'GEX updated 3 min ago').
how: The levels come from the GEX data for SPX, SPY, QQQ and GLD. On ES and MES charts the SPX levels are converted to the futures contract; NQ and MNQ use QQQ levels; GC and MGC use GLD levels. While the market is open, the futures conversion is re-anchored to the chart's own 1-minute futures bars at the time of the options data. The data is fetched every 5 minutes while the page is visible.

The main call wall, put wall and zero gamma use all expiries from 1 to 30 days. The Expiry setting picks the expiry for the IV range and the 0DTE walls. Ranked strikes are the biggest strikes by absolute GEX, tagged Support, Resistance, Magnet, Accelerant or Flip; these roles describe where dealer hedging may lean, not signals. Previous days' big levels show the two biggest strikes of each of the last recorded sessions (2 by default) as faded dotted lines.
use: Some traders watch how price behaves as it nears the call wall or put wall.
Use the zero gamma line to see where net gamma flips from positive to negative.
Some traders compare the IV 68% range with the day's actual range.
Use the previous days' strikes to see which big levels carried over.
Some traders read the GEX lines together with pPOC, pVAH and pVAL to see where options levels and volume levels line up.
notes: Works on SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, MES, NQ, MNQ, GC and MGC charts; other symbols show a short note and nothing is drawn.
Futures levels are converted from the index or ETF, so they are estimates of where those strikes sit on the contract.
In bar replay the levels come from the recorded GEX history as of the replay time; before the history begins the chart says so.
Session levels (pVAH, ONH and the rest) are drawn on futures charts only.

items.name: TradeZoro GEX Heatmap
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Net GEX at every strike through the session, drawn behind the candles (SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, NQ and gold GC)
items.summary: Paints net GEX at every strike, snapshot by snapshot, as a coloured heatmap under the candles for the last few sessions.
overview: TradeZoro GEX Heatmap shows how gamma exposure was spread across strikes through the session. Each row is a strike and each column is a 2-minute snapshot. Positive net GEX uses a mint and teal ramp, negative uses red and magenta, and values near zero stay clear so the candles show through.
By default it covers the last 3 sessions at 55% opacity, and a status note shows when the data was last updated (for example 'updated 3 min ago').
how: The heatmap is built from the recorded GEX history for SPX, SPY and QQQ. ES and MES use SPX strikes; NQ and MNQ use QQQ strikes scaled by the NDX/QQQ ratio. For futures, the price offset is taken per snapshot from the chart's own bar at that snapshot's time, so the heat lines up with the futures candles you see.

You can choose the expiry (0DTE or 1DTE), the number of sessions (1 to 5) and the opacity. In bar replay only snapshots up to the replay time are used, so nothing from later in the day leaks into the replay.
use: Some traders watch which strikes hold the strongest positive or negative GEX through the day.
Use it to see whether a big strike stayed in place or faded across snapshots.
Some traders compare where price paused with where the heat was strongest.
Use it next to GEX Levels to see how the current walls built up.
notes: Works on SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, MES, NQ and MNQ charts.
Data is recorded in 2-minute snapshots, so it cannot show changes inside a snapshot.
Before the recorded history begins, the chart reads 'No GEX history for this time'.

items.name: Dark Pool Prints
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Large off-exchange stock trades drawn at their exact price and time, sized by $ value; $10M+ highlighted. US stocks and ETFs, updated every 2 hours
items.summary: Draws large off-exchange stock trades (dark pool prints) at the exact price and time they printed, sized by dollar value, with $10M+ blocks highlighted.
overview: Dark Pool Prints puts each large trade that was reported off the exchanges on your stock chart, at the price and time it happened. Each print is a dot sized by its dollar value, with a label such as "$40M". Prints of $10M or more are filled in mint so the big blocks stand out.

Open the Dark pool list from the chart's right-hand bar (on a phone, the Dark pool button) to see the prints as a table: time, price, shares and value. Tap a row and the chart moves to that print and rings it.
how: US trades done away from the exchanges are reported to a regulator-run trade reporting facility, and each report carries that venue. TradeZoro reads the trade reports for the session, keeps the ones from those facilities worth $1M or more (price times shares), and stores the last five sessions. Each dot is one trade, not a total.

Some reports are not at the market price of that moment: average-price trades, contingent trades, derivatively priced trades and late reports. They are kept in the list with a star, and hidden from the chart unless you turn on "Show average-price / contingent prints". The size setting filters prints at $1M, $5M, $10M or $25M.
use: Some traders watch where big blocks traded relative to the day's range.
Use it to see whether large prints clustered near a level that price later came back to.
Some traders compare the prints with volume or VWAP on the same chart.
Use the $10M or $25M filter to keep only the largest blocks in view.
notes: US stocks and ETFs only, on a set list of 29 symbols including SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, AAPL, NVDA, MSFT and TSLA. Futures, crypto and forex show a short note instead.
Updated every 2 hours on US trading days; the chart shows when it was last updated (for example "updated 12 min ago").
A dark pool print shows that a trade happened at that price. It does not say who bought or sold, or why.
Nothing is drawn in bar replay.

items.name: Off-exchange levels (FINRA data)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Price levels where weekly off-exchange volume clustered (average price of the week). FINRA data, updated weekly
items.summary: Draws horizontal levels at the average price of each week's off-exchange volume, from public weekly off-exchange (dark pool / ATS) volume data, thicker where more shares traded.
overview: Off-exchange levels marks the prices where weekly off-exchange volume clustered for a stock or ETF. By default it shows the 5 most active levels. Line thickness follows the number of shares behind each level.
how: The data comes from a public weekly off-exchange (dark pool / ATS) volume summary: for each symbol and week, the shares and dollar value traded on ATS (dark pool) venues and other OTC. These files carry no price per trade, so the level for a week is its average price: dollar value divided by shares.

Weeks whose average prices sit within 0.5% of each other are merged into one level, and the levels are ranked by shares. The file is refreshed daily, but the weekly data is published about three weeks after the week ends.
use: Some traders watch how price reacts when it returns to a heavy off-exchange level.
Use it to see where large amounts of off-exchange volume changed hands in past weeks.
Some traders compare these levels with volume profile levels from the chart.
notes: Stocks and ETFs in the data file only (for example SPY, QQQ, AAPL); other symbols show a note.
A level is a weekly average price, not a single trade or print.
The weekly data lags by about three weeks, so the most recent weeks are not included.
The indicator does not say what the levels mean or which side traded.

items.name: Off-exchange Volume (FINRA data)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Daily off-exchange share of volume in a lower pane. FINRA data, updated daily
items.summary: Shows the daily share of a stock's volume reported off the exchanges, as a percentage line in a lower pane, from public daily off-exchange volume data.
overview: Off-exchange Volume draws one line in a pane below the chart: the percentage of each day's volume that was reported off-exchange (dark pool / ATS and other off-exchange trades), meaning trades done away from the exchanges. A status line shows when the data was refreshed.
how: The data comes from public daily off-exchange (dark pool / ATS) volume data, which lists the total off-exchange volume reported for each symbol each day. The indicator divides that by the chart's volume for the same day and plots the result in percent.
If the result would be above 100%, the chart's volume is not the consolidated count, so nothing is drawn for that day. The data file is refreshed once a day, in the US evening.
use: Some traders watch for days when the off-exchange share is unusually high or low for that stock.
Use it to see how much of a stock's trading happens away from the exchanges over time.
Some traders compare the share with price moves on the same days.
notes: Daily charts only.
Stocks and ETFs in the data file only (for example SPY, QQQ, AAPL).
It shows a share of volume, not the direction of the trades.

items.name: Options Flow Marks
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Bubbles on the candles where call (green) or put (red) premium was large, sized by premium; hover or tap for details. Per-bar totals, not single trades (SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, NQ)
items.summary: Places bubbles on candles where call premium (green, above) or put premium (red, below) was unusually large, sized by premium.
overview: Options Flow Marks highlights bars with heavy options premium. A green bubble above the candle marks large call premium; a red bubble below marks large put premium. Bigger bubbles mean more premium in that bar.
Hover or tap a bubble to see a card with calls or puts, the premium, the number of contracts and the net bought-minus-sold estimate. The card says plainly that strike and expiry are not in the data.
how: It uses the same per-minute options samples as ZoroTide for SPX, SPY and QQQ (ES and NQ charts map to SPX and QQQ). Samples are added up per chart bar, so each mark is a bar total across all contracts, not a single trade.

Within the visible bars, a bar qualifies when its call or put premium is in the top share for that side: 5% at Low sensitivity, 10% at Medium, 20% at High. The biggest marks are kept first, with at most one bubble every 3 bars. Bubble size scales with the square root of premium against the biggest mark.
use: Some traders watch where heavy call or put premium showed up during a move.
Use it to see whether options activity clustered near a high, a low or a breakout.
Some traders compare the bubbles with ZoroTide's running totals.
notes: Intraday charts only, on SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES and NQ.
Premium is estimated from options volume and quotes.
Nothing is drawn in bar replay, because the day's totals would show the future.
Strike and expiry are not available, so the marks do not show which contracts traded.

items.name: TradeZoro Earnings dates
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: An “E” on the day a US company reports earnings, with the EPS estimate on hover. Data updated daily
items.summary: Places an orange E on the day a US company reports earnings, with the timing and EPS estimate shown on hover.
overview: TradeZoro Earnings dates marks each earnings report on a US stock chart with a small E. Hover or tap it to see the date, whether the report comes before the open or after the close, the EPS estimate when one is available, and the fiscal quarter.
how: The dates come from an earnings file that is updated once a day. For the chart's ticker, each report is placed on the bar of its date: reports before the open sit at the US open, others after the close.
The only setting is the marker colour.
use: Some traders check the next report date before holding a stock overnight.
Use it to see how price moved around past earnings dates.
Some traders compare the size of gaps after each report.
notes: US stocks only; other charts show 'US stocks only'.
It shows dates and estimates, not the reported results.
The data is updated daily, so a date that changes today may not show until the next update.

items.name: TradeZoro Economic events
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: High-impact releases (CPI, FOMC, NFP, GDP…) as dashed lines, with a “CPI in 12 min” warning chip
items.summary: Draws dashed vertical lines at high-impact economic releases such as CPI, FOMC, NFP and GDP, with a countdown chip before the next one.
overview: TradeZoro Economic events marks scheduled releases on the chart. Each event gets a dashed vertical line and a short label (CPI, FOMC, NFP, GDP, PCE and others). When the next release is close, a warning chip appears in the chart header, for example 'CPI in 12 min'.
Hover or tap a line to see the country, the impact level, the full title, and the actual, forecast and previous values when they are available.
how: Events come from an economic calendar feed. By default it shows high-impact US events; you can switch to high and medium impact, and to US plus EU, UK, Japan and China. The warning chip shows when an event is within 30 minutes by default.
In bar replay, events after the replay time are not drawn and actual values are never shown; the chip counts down from the replay time.
use: Some traders use the chip as a reminder before a release.
Use the lines to see how price behaved around past CPI or FOMC releases.
Some traders avoid opening new positions just before high-impact events.
notes: Release times and values come from the calendar feed; they can change.
It marks events; it does not judge their effect on price.

items.name: TradeZoro Expected Move
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Options-implied expected move (ATM straddle) for 0DTE, 1DTE, weekly and monthly (SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, NQ)
items.summary: Draws the options-implied expected move for the chosen expiry as a shaded range with dashed edges and price tags on the chart.
overview: TradeZoro Expected Move shows the range the options market implies for an expiry. It draws a shaded box with dashed lines at the upper and lower edges and tags at the right edge. You can pick 0DTE, 1DTE, Weekly or Monthly, or show every expiry at once in its own colour.
A status line shows when the data was last updated (for example 'updated 3 min ago').
how: The expected move is based on the at-the-money straddle for the chosen expiry, computed on the server from the options chain for SPX, SPY and QQQ. ES and MES charts use the SPX range converted to the futures; NQ and MNQ use the QQQ range. The data is fetched every 5 minutes.
When the Weekly and Monthly entries point to the same expiry, they are shown as one range named 'Weekly / Monthly'.
use: Some traders compare the day's high and low with the 0DTE expected move.
Use it to see whether price is near or outside the implied range.
Some traders show every expiry at once to compare short and longer ranges.
notes: Works on SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, MES, NQ and MNQ.
Nothing is drawn in bar replay, because the range is today's.
The range is what options pricing implies, not a forecast of where price will go.

items.name: TradeZoro News markers
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Headline markers on the time axis for the chart’s market; hover or tap to read them
items.summary: Places small icons along the bottom of the chart at bars that had headlines for the chart's market; hover or tap to read them.
overview: TradeZoro News markers shows when news came out for the market you are looking at. A small icon sits at each bar that had headlines. On desktop, hovering shows the headlines; a tap or click opens a short list, and each row opens the article at its source.
how: Headlines come from a news feed, tagged by market: NQ, ES, YM, GC, SI, CL, BTC and ETH, plus the macro news that moves each. Related symbols map to these tags; for example MNQ, NDX and QQQ use NQ, and SPX and SPY use ES. Headlines are grouped into the chart's bars, newest first in each group.
In bar replay, no headline published after the replay time is shown.
use: Some traders check whether a sharp candle lined up with a headline.
Use it to scroll back and see what news came out around a move.
Some traders open the full article from the list to read the details.
notes: Covers the markets listed above; other symbols may show no markers.
It shows headlines and short summaries, not full articles.
It does not rate the news or its effect on price.

items.name: ZoroTide (options money flow: calls vs puts)
items.windowName: ZoroTide (options money flow: calls vs puts)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Options money flow: net call premium (green) vs net put premium (red) since the open, in a lower pane (SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, NQ)
items.summary: Plots net call premium (green) and net put premium (red) since the 9:30 ET open as two running lines in a lower pane.
overview: ZoroTide shows options money flow for the day. In a pane below the chart, the green line is the running net call premium and the red line is the running net put premium, both in dollars, starting from the 9:30 ET open. A status line shows when it was last updated.
how: The data comes from per-minute samples built from the options chains for SPX, SPY and QQQ (ES and MES map to SPX, NQ and MNQ to QQQ). For each contract, new volume is the volume now minus the previous sample, and premium is new volume times price times 100 (last trade, otherwise mid).

A last trade in the top 25% of the bid-ask spread counts as bought, in the bottom 25% as sold, and in between as half and half. Net is bought minus sold, and the lines add the samples up from the open. Each bar shows the totals at its close; gaps longer than 20 minutes are left blank.
use: Some traders watch whether the call and put lines are moving apart or coming together.
Use it to see whether price moves line up with options money flow.
Some traders compare the slope of each line through the session.
notes: Works on SPX, SPY, QQQ, ES, MES, NQ and MNQ.
The bought and sold split is estimated from options volume and quotes.
Nothing is drawn in bar replay, because the day's totals would show the future.

items.name: SMT Divergence Pro [TradeZoro]
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: SMT divergence vs correlated futures (auto-paired: NQ vs ES), chart TF + higher TFs
items.summary: Joins two swing points with a line where one correlated futures market makes a new swing and the other fails to, on several timeframes.
overview: SMT Divergence Pro compares your chart with a correlated instrument. When one makes a new swing high or low and the other does not, the two swing points are joined by a line, with a small up or down marker at the divergence. Bullish SMT is read from swing lows and bearish SMT from swing highs.

It runs on the chart timeframe plus up to three higher timeframes, each with its own pivot strength, colours and number of past SMTs kept (20 by default). A watermark lists the symbols and timeframes in use.
how: With auto-pair on, NQ is compared with ES, ES with NQ, and YM and RTY with ES. With it off you can set up to three comparison symbols yourself. Swings are found on both symbols independently, so a divergence is caught whichever instrument prints the pivot. Pivot strength Weak, Medium and Strong mean 2, 5 and 10 candles either side, or a custom number.

Higher-timeframe candles are built from the chart's own bars, so each line is anchored to the exact chart bar that made the swing. While a swing is still forming, a provisional dotted line can be drawn and is then replaced on confirmation or removed if the pivot fails. When price later trades through the divergence swing, the SMT is removed by default, or kept dimmed. An optional session filter limits detection to set time windows.
use: Some traders look for SMT near a session high or low as a sign one market is not confirming the other.
Use the higher-timeframe lines to see divergences that the chart timeframe alone would miss.
Some traders combine it with liquidity sweeps or fair value gaps from other tools.
Use the session filter to study only the hours you trade.
notes: Needs data for the comparison symbol on the same timeframe.
Higher timeframes must be above the chart timeframe.
A divergence is a comparison of swings, not a signal on its own.

items.name: IFVG Pro+ [TradeZoro]
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Liquidity (BSL / SSL from higher-TF swings and candles), sweep, candidate FVG and inversion (IFVG) boxes, risk / reward box
items.summary: Marks buyside and sellside liquidity from higher timeframes, the sweep of a level, the fair value gap in that leg and its inversion (IFVG).
overview: IFVG Pro+ follows one sequence. It draws buyside (BSL) and sellside (SSL) liquidity lines from higher-timeframe swings and candle highs and lows. When a level is swept, it finds the most recent chart-timeframe fair value gap inside the leg into that level and shows it as a candidate box. If price then closes back through that gap, the gap is marked as an inversion fair value gap (IFVG).

An optional risk and reward box can be drawn from the IFVG, with the stop at the sweep wick and the target at the R multiple you choose. Setups that hit the stop before 1R are marked failed and hidden by default.
how: With auto-select on, liquidity comes from the two timeframes directly above your chart; you can also pick 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h or daily by hand. Swing strength is 2 candles either side and 10 levels are kept each side by default. Higher-timeframe candles are built from completed chart bars, without looking ahead.

By default a sweep means a wick through the level with a close back inside; you can switch to a close through, or either. With leg-extreme liquidity on, only the high or low that ends a price leg counts, and the leg into it must be at least 1 ATR (14). The gap search looks back up to 150 bars and waits up to 40 bars for the inversion. A bias setting and a session filter (Asia, London, New York) narrow which setups show.
use: Some traders use it to see the sweep-then-inversion pattern in one place.
Use the dimmed swept lines to review which liquidity was already taken.
Some traders study the risk and reward box to see how past setups played out.
Use the bias and session settings to focus on one direction or time of day.
notes: The chart timeframe must be below the liquidity timeframes for them to draw.
The risk and reward box is a study aid, not an order.
Gap size can be filtered in ticks; 0 turns the filter off.

items.name: HTF PO3 Lens [TradeZoro]
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Up to five higher-timeframe candles drawn right of the last bar, with HTF FVGs, sweeps and a countdown to the close
items.summary: Draws candles from up to five higher timeframes to the right of the last bar, with their fair value gaps, sweeps and a countdown to each close.
overview: HTF PO3 Lens lets you read higher-timeframe candles without leaving your chart. To the right of the last bar it draws a stack of candles for each chosen timeframe, lined up with the chart's price scale. By default it shows two candles each for 15m, 1h and 4h; daily and weekly can be switched on.

Each stack carries its timeframe name and a countdown to the candle close. Fair value gaps between the stacked candles are shaded, and sweeps of a prior candle's high or low are marked with a short line across the wick that took it.
how: The higher-timeframe candles are built from completed chart bars, with no lookahead. You set how many candles per timeframe (1 to 6), the distance from the last bar, the candle width and the gaps between candles and stacks.

A fair value gap is the space left between candles in the stack, and it can be extended to the end of the stack. Sweeps shown per stack default to the most recent one. Optional extras add BSL or SSL text beside the sweep marker and extend swept levels back across the chart as dashed lines. A price line runs across the panel at the current price.
use: Some traders read the open, high, low and close of the higher-timeframe candle to frame the session (the Power of Three idea).
Use the countdown to see how much time is left in each higher-timeframe candle.
Some traders watch whether price is trading into a higher-timeframe gap.
Use the sweep marks to see which candle highs or lows were taken.
notes: The chosen timeframes should be above the chart timeframe.
The stack sits in the space right of the last bar, so leave room on the chart.
The script has no alert conditions.

items.name: FVG Relay [TradeZoro]
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Higher-timeframe FVGs on your chart; tapped and respected gaps chain as Relay 1, 2, 3; liquidity and dashboard
items.summary: Draws higher-timeframe fair value gaps on your chart and chains each tapped and respected gap as Relay 1, 2, 3 until the chain breaks.
overview: FVG Relay puts higher-timeframe fair value gaps on the chart you trade from. When price taps a gap and closes back in the gap's direction, that gap becomes Relay 1 and sets the trend. Each later gap that is tapped and respected adds to the chain as Relay 2, Relay 3 and so on.

Each relay draws a target line to the next resting liquidity level in its direction. A dashboard in the top right shows the timeframes, the trend, relays in the chain, open gaps, chains and the best chain, and targets reached.
how: Gaps come from 15m by default; 5m, 1h and 4h can be added, or all at once. Where a lower-timeframe gap overlaps a higher one, only the higher one is drawn. Higher-timeframe candles are built from completed chart bars with no lookahead. Up to 8 open gaps are drawn.

By default a bounce is confirmed when a bar closes back through the gap's near edge; you can switch to a close beyond the tap candle's extreme. The chain ends when a higher-timeframe candle closes through the far side of a relay gap, and the chart starts clean. Resting liquidity is read from 5m swings (strength 2) with 12 levels kept each side.
use: Some traders use the relay count to see how long a trend has kept respecting gaps.
Use the target lines to see the next liquidity level in the trend direction.
Some traders watch for the chain-broken event as a change in conditions.
Use the dashboard to review chains and targets reached on the visible history.
notes: Gap timeframes must be above the chart timeframe.
Gaps older than the current chain are removed.
The dashboard counts what happened on the loaded history only.

items.name: TZ Fractal Model [TradeZoro]
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Fractal HTF sweep model with right-side candles, CISD confirmation, projections and dashboard
items.summary: Marks a higher-timeframe candle that sweeps the prior candle's high or low and closes back, then CISD confirmation, projections and right-side candles.
overview: TZ Fractal Model pairs a lower and a higher timeframe and looks for one pattern. A higher-timeframe candle (C2) trades beyond the prior candle's (C1) low or high and closes back inside it. The model then waits for a change in state of delivery (CISD) on the chart: a close back through the open of the run of candles that made the extreme.

When confirmed, it draws the CISD line, projection lines, the C2 midpoint (EQ), a T-spot box, the C1 liquidity ray and nearby formation liquidity. C2, C3 and C4 labels mark the candles; they turn red if the setup fails. Higher-timeframe candles are also drawn to the right of the last bar, with an info table.
how: Pairing is automatic from the chart timeframe (for example 5m with 1H) or set by hand: 1m-15m, 3m-30m, 5m-1H, 15m-4H, 1H-1D or 4H-1W. Higher-timeframe candles are built from chart bars with no lookahead.

A setup fails if price returns beyond the C2 extreme. If confirmation comes after the next higher-timeframe candle, the labels show in the no-fail colour. Projections are multiples of the leg from the C2 extreme to the CISD level: 1, 2, 2.5, 4 and 4.5 by default. The info table shows the model name, a countdown to the higher-timeframe close, the bias and whether the time filter is on. Up to three New York time windows can limit where setups form.
use: Some traders use it to study higher-timeframe sweeps from a lower-timeframe chart.
Use the CISD line to see where the lower timeframe changed direction.
Some traders use the projection lines as reference levels for the move.
Use the history setting to review recent setups that held or failed.
notes: If the chart timeframe is above the pair's lower timeframe, only the higher-timeframe candles are drawn.
The bias setting limits setups to one direction.
The script has no alert conditions.

items.name: Liquidity Master [TradeZoro]
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Session, previous day / week / month, swing and candle liquidity per timeframe, HTF FVGs, REQH / REQL and draw-on-liquidity tables
items.summary: Draws session, previous day, week and month highs and lows, swing and candle liquidity per timeframe, HTF fair value gaps and REQH / REQL.
overview: Liquidity Master gathers the places liquidity can rest onto one chart. It draws fair value gaps from the chart and higher timeframes, swing highs and lows per timeframe, completed candle highs and lows, Asia, London and New York session highs and lows, and previous day and week highs and lows (previous month is optional).

Two draw-on-liquidity tables list the nearest unswept major highs above price and lows below. It can also mark relative equal highs and lows (REQH and REQL), opening price lines (09:30 and 10:00 by default) and low-resistance legs.
how: Liquidity lines run from the bar that made them until the wick that takes them, then stop. Session and period lines also end at their natural expiry. Fair value gaps are removed when a candle closes through the far side, and where gaps overlap the highest timeframe wins. All higher-timeframe candles are built from chart bars, so each level is anchored to the bar that made it.

By default gaps show for the chart, 15m and 1h, swing liquidity for 5m, 15m and 1h, and candle liquidity for 1h and 4h, limited to the last 40 lines and to levels formed today and yesterday. The trading day starts at 18:00 New York time. Labels for levels close together are merged, for example NY Low and PDL, within 40% of ATR by default.
use: Some traders use the tables to see the nearest untaken highs and lows at a glance.
Use the session lines to see which session's high or low has been swept.
Some traders watch equal highs or lows as places stops may rest.
Use the timeframe switches to keep only the levels you study.
notes: It draws many objects; turning off timeframes you do not need keeps the chart readable.
Higher timeframes are built from the loaded chart bars, so a short history limits them.
The script has no alert conditions.

items.name: Session Sweep SMT + IFVG [TradeZoro]
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Session and previous day highs / lows, the sweep of each, SMT against the correlated symbol, and the IFVG that follows. Marks only.
items.summary: Marks session and previous-day highs and lows, the sweep of each, SMT against the correlated symbol and the IFVG that follows.
overview: Session Sweep SMT + IFVG marks one model step by step. It draws Asia, London and NY AM session highs and lows (NY PM is optional) and the previous day high and low, each running right until swept. A sweep stops the line and places a small swept mark on the wick.

If the correlated symbol did not take its own level for the same session, the sweep has SMT and a dashed line joins the two swing points. After that, the first fair value gap against the move that price closes through is boxed as the IFVG. When all three happen, a compact tag sits on the IFVG candle.
how: A sweep is a candle trading through a level by at least one tick. With auto-pair on, NQ is compared with ES, MNQ with MES, ES with NQ, YM and RTY with ES, SPX with NDX, and GC with SI; otherwise you set the symbol. Sessions use New York time by default, and the trading day starts at 18:00.

The IFVG must come within 20 bars of the sweep, be at least 2 ticks, and may start up to 10 bars before the sweep. By default an IFVG is marked only after a sweep with SMT. Everything is drawn on closed candles. Open levels farther than 0.5% from price are hidden until price gets close, and 5 days of history are shown.
use: Some traders use it to study how often a session sweep is followed by SMT and an IFVG.
Use the swept marks to see which session levels were taken today.
Some traders turn on the table to see today's sessions in one place.
Use partial sequences to review sweeps that did not complete the model.
notes: Needs data for the correlated symbol.
It only marks the chart; it does not place orders.
Partial sequences show only the parts that happened.

items.name: EMA 9/21 cross
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Plots a fast 9-period and slow 21-period EMA on the chart and marks each point where the fast line crosses the slow one.
overview: EMA 9/21 cross is a short example Pine script. It draws two exponential moving averages on the price chart: a fast EMA in teal and a slow EMA in orange. A small teal triangle below the bar marks a cross up, and an orange triangle above the bar marks a cross down.
how: Both lines are standard exponential moving averages of the close, with lengths 9 and 21 by default. A cross up is the bar where the fast EMA moves above the slow EMA; a cross down is the bar where it moves below. You can change both lengths.
use: Some traders use the cross as a simple way to see a change in short-term direction.
Use the gap between the two lines to see how strong the trend is.
Some traders watch for price pulling back to the slow EMA during a trend.
Use it as a starting point to learn how Pine scripts plot lines and markers.
notes: Moving averages lag price, so crosses appear after the move has started.
In sideways markets the lines can cross back and forth often.
The script has no alert conditions.

items.name: Exponential Moving Average
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: A single exponential moving average line on the price chart, 20 bars on the close by default, weighted toward recent bars.
overview: The Exponential Moving Average (EMA) draws one smooth line over price. It reacts faster than a simple average of the same length because recent bars carry more weight.
By default it uses 20 bars of closing prices and is drawn in blue. You can change the source, shift the line with an offset, and pick its color.
how: Each new value is the previous EMA plus a share of the gap between the latest price and that EMA. The share is 2 / (Length + 1), so with a length of 20 each bar moves the line about 9.5% of the way toward price.
Older bars never drop out completely; their influence fades smoothly over time.
use: Some traders watch whether price is above or below the line to judge the short-term trend.
Use its slope to see if momentum is building or fading.
Pair two EMAs of different lengths and watch where they cross.
Some traders treat the line as a moving area of support or resistance in a trend.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Like any average it lags price, so turns show up after they start.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Least Squares Moving Average
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Least squares moving average: the end point of a straight-line fit over the last 25 bars, colored by its slope.
overview: The Least Squares Moving Average (LSMA) fits a straight line through the last 25 closes on every bar and plots where that line ends. The result tracks price more closely than a simple average of the same length.
With Slope Trend Coloring on, the line turns green while rising, red while falling and gray when flat.
how: On each bar the indicator runs a linear regression on the last N values (25 by default) and plots the fitted value at the current bar. Regression Offset steps back along the fitted line: 0 uses the end point, larger values read the line further back for a smoother result.
Because it follows the fitted trend, it can lead turns that a same-length SMA trails, but it can overshoot after sharp moves.
use: Use the color change to see when the fitted trend flips direction.
Some traders compare price with the LSMA to see how far it has stretched from its recent trend.
Use it as a faster alternative to an SMA of the same length.
Watch a flat gray line as a sign of a pause in trend.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It can overshoot after sudden moves because it projects the recent slope.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Moving Average
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: One or two moving averages in one study, with 13 types to choose from, including SMA, EMA, HMA, ALMA, KAMA and VWMA.
overview: This study draws one moving average, or two if you turn on MA 2. Each line has its own type, length and source. By default MA 1 is a 20-bar SMA in blue and MA 2 is a 50-bar SMA in orange.
It lets you compare average types without adding a separate indicator for each one.
how: The types are SMA, EMA, WMA, RMA (SMMA), HMA, ALMA, VWMA, DEMA, TEMA, KAMA, LSMA, McGinley and Hamming. Each is the standard formula: for example SMA is a plain average, EMA weights recent bars more, VWMA weights by volume, and HMA combines weighted averages to cut lag.
ALMA uses an offset (0.85) and sigma (6) to shape its window. LSMA has its own regression offset. A global offset shifts both lines.
use: Some traders watch a fast and a slow line and note when they cross.
Use it to see how different average types react to the same move.
Watch price relative to the 50-bar line as a broad trend filter.
Use the slope of each line to see if the trend is speeding up or slowing.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
VWMA needs volume data.
All averages lag price to some degree.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Moving Average Envelope
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: A moving average with upper and lower bands set a fixed percent away, 2.5% around a 20-bar SMA by default.
overview: The Moving Average Envelope draws a basis moving average with two bands, one above and one below, at a fixed percentage distance. By default the basis is a 20-bar SMA of the close and the bands sit 2.5% away.
Colors follow direction: bullish and bearish colors, with a gray basis.
how: Upper band = basis x (1 + percent / 100). Lower band = basis x (1 - percent / 100). The basis can be SMA, EMA, WMA, RMA (SMMA), HMA or VWMA.
Unlike Bollinger Bands, the width does not change with volatility; it is always the same share of the basis.
use: Some traders watch touches of the bands as signs price is stretched from its average.
Use a close outside the band to spot strong moves.
Use the basis as the trend line and the bands as a range around it.
Adjust the percent to fit how much the symbol usually moves.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
A fixed percent may be too wide on quiet symbols and too narrow on volatile ones.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Simple Moving Average
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: A single simple moving average line on the price chart: the plain average of the last 20 closes by default.
overview: The Simple Moving Average (SMA) draws one line that is the plain average of the last N values. By default it averages 20 closing prices and is drawn in blue.
You can change the source, shift the line with an offset, and pick its color.
how: SMA = sum of the last N values / N. Each bar in the window counts the same, and the oldest bar drops out when a new one arrives.
Because every bar weighs the same, the SMA is smoother but slower to react than an EMA of the same length.
use: Some traders watch whether price closes above or below the line.
Use its slope to read the direction of the trend.
Add a second SMA of another length and watch where they cross.
Some traders use well-known lengths like 50 or 200 as broad trend references.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The line can jump when a large bar drops out of the window.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Smoothed Moving Average
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Smoothed (Wilder) moving average, 14 bars by default, a slow and steady line colored by its slope.
overview: The Smoothed Moving Average, also called RMA or Wilder's average, draws a slow and steady line over price. It is the same smoothing used inside RSI and ATR.
With Slope Trend Coloring on, the line is green while rising, red while falling and gray when flat. Length is 14 by default.
how: Each new value = (previous value x (N - 1) + latest price) / N. This works like an EMA with a smoothing share of 1 / N instead of 2 / (N + 1), so it reacts more slowly than an EMA of the same length.
The first value is seeded with a simple average.
use: Use it as a calm trend line that ignores small swings.
Some traders watch the color change as a sign the trend has turned.
Compare it with an EMA of the same length to see how much smoothing changes the picture.
Use it as a longer-term trend filter on lower timeframes.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It lags more than an EMA of the same length.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Variable Index Dynamic Average
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: VIDYA: an adaptive moving average that speeds up in strong moves and slows in quiet ones, colored by trend regime.
overview: The Variable Index Dynamic Average (VIDYA) is a moving average whose speed changes bar by bar. It moves faster when momentum is strong and almost stops when the market is quiet.
With Trend Regime Coloring on, it is green while sloping up, red while sloping down and gray when flat. The adaptive gradient fades the color as momentum dies.
how: VIDYA starts from an EMA smoothing share of 2 / (N + 1), with N = 12 by default, and multiplies it by a scaler each bar. In Momentum mode the scaler is the absolute Chande Momentum Oscillator (9 bars) divided by 100. In Volatility mode it is a short standard deviation divided by a reference standard deviation (30 bars).
The line counts as flat when its one-bar change is below 0.05 of ATR(14).
use: Use the flat color to spot ranges where the average stops moving.
Some traders watch the regime color change as a sign of a new trend.
Use it as a trend line that stays still in noise.
Compare Momentum and Volatility modes to see which suits the symbol.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It can stay flat for long periods in quiet markets.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Williams Alligator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Williams Alligator: three smoothed averages of median price, shifted forward, called the jaw, teeth and lips.
overview: The Williams Alligator draws three lines on the price chart. The jaw (purple) is slow, the teeth (orange) are medium and the lips (yellow) are fast. Each one is pushed forward in time by a few bars.
When the lines are tangled, the market is often ranging. When they fan out in order, price is trending.
how: Each line is a smoothed moving average (SMMA) of median price, (high + low) / 2. Classic settings: jaw 13 bars shifted 8, teeth 8 bars shifted 5, lips 5 bars shifted 3.
The forward shift means the last few bars of each line extend past the current candle.
use: Some traders read tangled lines as the Alligator sleeping and stay patient.
Watch the lines spread apart in order (lips, teeth, jaw) as a sign of a trend.
Use price crossing the jaw as a broad trend change signal.
Pair it with the Gator Oscillator to see the spread as a histogram.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The forward shift is part of the design; it is not a forecast.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Zero-Lag Exponential Moving Average
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Zero-lag EMA: an exponential average with a de-lag step, 21 bars by default, colored by slope.
overview: The Zero-Lag Exponential Moving Average (ZLEMA) is an EMA that tries to cancel most of the usual delay. It hugs price more closely than a plain EMA of the same length.
With Slope Trend Coloring on, it is green while rising, red while falling and gray when flat. Length is 21 by default.
how: An EMA of length N lags by about (N - 1) / 2 bars. ZLEMA first builds a de-lagged source: price + (price - price from that many bars ago). It then takes an EMA of that series with a smoothing share of 2 / (N + 1).
The extra step adds recent momentum back in, which reduces lag but can cause small overshoots.
use: Use it as a faster trend line than a standard EMA.
Some traders watch the color flip as an early sign of a turn.
Compare it with a normal EMA to see how much lag is removed.
Use it on lower timeframes where quick response matters.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It can overshoot after sharp moves.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Awesome Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Awesome Oscillator histogram: 5-bar minus 34-bar simple average of median price, green when rising and red when falling.
overview: The Awesome Oscillator shows momentum as a histogram in its own pane, around a zero line. Bars are green when the value is higher than on the previous bar and red when lower or equal.
It was created by Bill Williams to compare recent momentum with a longer view.
how: AO = SMA(median price, 5) - SMA(median price, 34), where median price = (high + low) / 2.
Above zero, the short-term average is above the long-term one; below zero, it is under it.
use: Some traders watch zero-line crosses as a sign of a change in momentum.
Look at the color sequence: a run of green bars shows momentum building.
Some traders look for a saucer pattern: three bars that dip and turn on the same side of zero.
Compare two peaks on the same side of zero with price peaks to look for divergence.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The 5 and 34 lengths are fixed in the classic formula.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Balance of Power
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Balance of Power: where each candle closed relative to its open, scaled by its range, from -1 to +1.
overview: Balance of Power (BOP) shows who controlled each bar. Values near +1 mean buyers pushed price from open to high; values near -1 mean sellers pushed it from open to low.
It plots in its own pane around zero, green above and red below. You can turn on smoothing for a calmer line.
how: BOP = (close - open) / (high - low). A bar with no range gives zero.
With Smoothing on, the raw value is passed through a simple moving average of the chosen length (14 by default).
use: Some traders watch the smoothed line crossing zero as a change in who controls the bars.
Use long runs above or below zero to see steady buying or selling.
Compare BOP with price to see if a new high is made with weaker bars.
Turn smoothing off to inspect single candles.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The raw form is noisy; most readers use the smoothed line.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Chande Momentum Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Chande Momentum Oscillator: net up moves versus down moves over 9 bars, from -100 to +100, with levels at plus and minus 50.
overview: The Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO) measures momentum on a scale from -100 to +100 in its own pane. Overbought and oversold levels sit at +50 and -50 by default.
The line and fill are green while momentum is positive and red while negative.
how: Over the last 9 bars, add all up moves (Su) and all down moves (Sd) of the source. CMO = 100 x (Su - Sd) / (Su + Sd).
Unlike RSI it uses raw sums without smoothing, so it reacts quickly.
use: Some traders watch moves beyond +50 or -50 as stretched conditions.
Use zero-line crosses to see changes in momentum direction.
Look for divergence between CMO and price at swing points.
Use its absolute value as a measure of trend strength.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Short lengths make it jumpy; longer ones smooth it.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Commodity Channel Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Commodity Channel Index: how far typical price sits from its 20-bar average, in units of mean deviation, with plus and minus 100 levels.
overview: The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) shows how far price has moved from its average, in its own pane. Reference levels sit at +100 and -100.
The line and fill are green above zero and red below.
how: CCI = (source - SMA(source, 20)) / (0.015 x mean absolute deviation). The source is typical price, (high + low + close) / 3, by default.
The 0.015 constant scales the result so most readings fall between -100 and +100.
use: Some traders read moves above +100 as strong upside and below -100 as strong downside.
Use returns inside the levels to see a move losing pace.
Watch zero-line crosses for changes in direction.
Look for divergence between CCI and price.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
CCI has no fixed upper or lower limit.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Connors RSI
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Connors RSI: average of a 3-bar RSI, a streak RSI and a 100-bar percent rank of returns, with levels at 90 and 10.
overview: Connors RSI (CRSI) is a short-term oscillator from 0 to 100 in its own pane. It blends three parts into one line. Levels sit at 90 (overbought) and 10 (oversold).
The line shifts toward red near overbought and green near oversold.
how: CRSI = (RSI(close, 3) + RSI(streak, 2) + PercentRank(1-bar ROC, 100)) / 3.
The streak counts how many bars in a row closed up (positive) or down (negative). PercentRank shows where today's one-bar change sits among the last 100.
use: Some traders watch readings under 10 or over 90 as short-term stretched conditions.
Use it on daily charts to spot short pullbacks within a trend.
Pair it with a longer trend filter so you read it in context.
Watch how quickly it leaves extreme zones.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is built for short swings and moves fast.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Coppock Curve
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Coppock Curve: a 10-bar weighted average of the sum of a 14-bar and an 11-bar rate of change, around zero.
overview: The Coppock Curve is a slow momentum line in its own pane. It was first made for monthly charts to spot the end of long declines.
The line and fill are green above zero and red below.
how: Coppock = WMA(ROC(source, 14) + ROC(source, 11), 10). ROC is the percent change from that many bars ago.
The original used monthly closes; here the lengths are in chart bars. Because the weighted average favors recent values, the curve turns a little sooner than a simple average would.
use: Some traders watch an upturn from below zero as a sign of recovering momentum.
Use zero-line crosses as broad momentum changes.
Use it on weekly or monthly charts as in its original design.
Compare its slope with price to see momentum fading.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is slow by design and better suited to higher timeframes.
It is not built to mark tops; its original use was spotting the end of declines.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Detrended Price Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Detrended Price Oscillator: price minus a shifted 21-bar average, to show short cycles without the trend.
overview: The Detrended Price Oscillator (DPO) removes the longer trend so you can see shorter cycles. It plots in its own pane around zero, green above and red below.
With Centered on, the line is shifted back so it lines up with the prices it measures.
how: DPO = source - SMA(source, 21) taken from 21 / 2 + 1 bars earlier. In centered mode the line is moved back by that many bars, so the newest bars show no value.
It compares price with an older value of the average, not the current one.
use: Use peaks and troughs to estimate the length of recent cycles.
Some traders watch zero crossings to time swings inside a range.
Use the centered view to study past cycles, and the default view for the latest bars.
Compare cycle highs with price highs.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is not built to show trend direction.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Elder Ray
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Elder Ray: Bull Power (high minus 13 EMA) and Bear Power (low minus 13 EMA) as two histograms.
overview: Elder Ray, by Alexander Elder, shows the strength of buyers and sellers in its own pane. Bull Power is drawn in green and Bear Power in red, both around zero.
It compares each bar's high and low with a 13-bar exponential moving average of closes.
how: Bull Power = high - EMA(close, 13). Bear Power = low - EMA(close, 13).
Bull Power above zero means the bar's high cleared the average; Bear Power below zero means its low went under it.
use: Some traders use the EMA slope for the trend and Bear Power for dips in an uptrend.
Watch Bull Power shrinking while price makes new highs as a sign of weaker buying.
Watch Bear Power rising toward zero in a downtrend as easing selling.
Use both bars together to see the range of each candle around the average.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is usually read together with the trend of the EMA itself.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Fisher Transform
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Fisher Transform: median price turned into a sharp oscillator over 9 bars, with a one-bar trigger line.
overview: The Fisher Transform, by John Ehlers, turns price into a line with clear peaks and troughs. It plots in its own pane with a trigger line, which is the Fisher line from one bar earlier.
Colors follow direction: green while the Fisher line is above the trigger, red while below.
how: First, median price (high + low) / 2 is placed in its 9-bar high-low range and scaled to between -1 and +1, with some smoothing. Then Fisher = 0.5 x ln((1 + x) / (1 - x)), also smoothed with its prior value.
This stretches values near the edges, so turning points stand out.
use: Some traders watch the Fisher line crossing its trigger as a turn signal.
Use extreme readings as a sign a move is stretched.
Look at how sharp the peaks are to see how strong a swing was.
Pair it with a trend filter to avoid reading every swing.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It reacts fast and can give many turns in choppy markets.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Gator Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Gator Oscillator: two histograms showing how far the Alligator's jaw, teeth and lips are spreading or converging.
overview: The Gator Oscillator shows the Williams Alligator as two histograms around zero. The upper bars show the gap between jaw and teeth; the lower bars show the gap between teeth and lips.
Bars are green when a gap is growing and red when it is shrinking. Color shows expansion, not direction.
how: Upper = |jaw - teeth|. Lower = -|teeth - lips|. Each line is a smoothed (Wilder) average of median price (high + low) / 2, using jaw 13 shifted 8, teeth 8 shifted 5 and lips 5 shifted 3.
The source and the average type can be changed.
use: Some traders read green bars on both sides as the Alligator eating: a trend in progress.
Watch red bars on both sides as the lines coming together.
Use mixed colors as a sign of a phase change.
Pair it with the Alligator on price for the direction.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It does not tell you up or down; check price or the Alligator for that.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Know Sure Thing
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Know Sure Thing: a weighted blend of four smoothed rates of change, with a 9-bar signal line.
overview: The Know Sure Thing (KST), by Martin Pring, combines momentum from four time spans into one line in its own pane, with a signal line in orange.
Colors show direction: green while KST is above its signal, red while below.
how: Take four rates of change (10, 15, 20 and 30 bars) and smooth them with simple averages (10, 10, 10 and 15). KST = RCMA1 x 1 + RCMA2 x 2 + RCMA3 x 3 + RCMA4 x 4.
The signal line is a 9-bar SMA of KST.
use: Some traders watch KST crossing its signal line as a change in momentum.
Use zero-line crosses as broader momentum shifts.
Look for divergence between KST and price.
Use it on higher timeframes for a long-term momentum view.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is smooth and slow; turns appear after price has moved.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Linear Regression Slope
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Linear regression slope: the slope of a straight-line fit over the last 100 bars, green when rising and red when falling.
overview: The Linear Regression Slope shows how steep the recent trend is, in its own pane. Above zero the fitted line points up; below zero it points down.
Colors show whether the slope is rising or falling from the previous bar.
how: On each bar a least-squares line is fitted to the last N values (100 by default). The plotted value is that line's slope: price change per bar.
The larger the absolute value, the steeper the fitted trend.
use: Use zero crossings to see when the fitted trend flips direction.
Some traders watch a falling slope while price rises as a sign the trend is tiring.
Use shorter lengths for swings and longer ones for the main trend.
Compare the slope across symbols with care, since it is in price units.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Values are in price per bar, so they differ by symbol.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: MACD
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: MACD: the 12 EMA minus the 26 EMA, a 9-bar signal line and a histogram showing the gap between the two lines.
overview: MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) shows momentum in its own pane. It has a blue MACD line, an orange signal line and a histogram.
Histogram bars are bright when the gap is growing and faded when it is shrinking, green above zero and red below.
how: MACD line = EMA(close, 12) - EMA(close, 26). Signal = EMA(MACD, 9). Histogram = MACD - Signal.
Above zero, the fast average is above the slow one.
use: Some traders watch the MACD line crossing the signal line as a change in momentum.
Use zero-line crosses to see the fast and slow averages swap places.
Look for divergence between MACD peaks and price peaks.
Watch the histogram shrink as an early sign a move is slowing.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Values are in price units, so they are not directly comparable across symbols.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Percentage Price Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Percentage Price Oscillator: the gap between a 12 and 26 EMA as a percent of the slow EMA, with signal line and histogram.
overview: The Percentage Price Oscillator (PPO) works like MACD but shows the gap as a percentage. That makes it easier to compare across symbols and price levels.
It plots in its own pane with a signal line, an optional histogram and a gradient fill.
how: PPO = (fast MA - slow MA) / slow MA x 100, with fast 12 and slow 26 EMAs by default. Signal = 9-bar EMA of PPO. Histogram = PPO - Signal.
The average types for the lines and the signal can be changed.
use: Some traders watch PPO crossing its signal line.
Use zero-line crosses as trend changes in the averages.
Compare PPO readings across symbols because it is in percent.
Watch for divergence between PPO and price.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It lags like any average-based tool.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Rate of Change
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Rate of Change: percent change from 9 bars ago, or the raw difference in Momentum mode, around a zero line.
overview: Rate of Change (ROC) shows how much price has moved over a set number of bars, in its own pane. Above zero price is higher than it was; below zero it is lower.
The line and gradient fill are green above zero and red below.
how: ROC % = (source - source 9 bars ago) / source 9 bars ago x 100. In Momentum mode it shows the raw difference instead.
The length sets how far back the comparison goes.
use: Some traders watch zero-line crosses as changes in short-term direction.
Use extreme readings to spot moves that are unusually fast for the symbol.
Look for divergence between ROC and price at swing points.
Use percent mode to compare symbols.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It can be jumpy because it compares only two points.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Relative Strength Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Relative Strength Index: Wilder RSI over 14 bars from 0 to 100, with overbought at 70 and oversold at 30.
overview: The Relative Strength Index (RSI) shows momentum on a scale from 0 to 100 in its own pane. Levels sit at 70 (overbought) and 30 (oversold), with a shaded band between.
The line takes the overbought or oversold color as it reaches those zones.
how: Over 14 bars, average gains and average losses are smoothed with Wilder's method (RMA). RS = average gain / average loss. RSI = 100 - 100 / (1 + RS).
When gains and losses are equal, RSI is 50.
use: Some traders watch readings above 70 or below 30 as stretched conditions.
Use the 50 line to separate up momentum from down momentum.
Look for divergence: price makes a new high while RSI does not.
In strong trends RSI can stay in a zone; some traders read that as strength, not a turn.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Overbought does not mean price must fall.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Relative Vigor Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Relative Vigor Index: the close-minus-open move compared with the bar range over 10 bars, with a signal line.
overview: The Relative Vigor Index (RVGI) compares where bars close relative to where they open, in its own pane. In up moves, closes tend to be above opens; in down moves, below.
It shows an RVGI line in green and a signal line in red.
how: Numerator = (close - open) smoothed with weights 1, 2, 2, 1 over four bars. Denominator = (high - low) smoothed the same way. RVGI = sum of numerators / sum of denominators over 10 bars.
Signal = RVGI smoothed with the same 1, 2, 2, 1 weights.
use: Some traders watch RVGI crossing its signal line.
Use readings above zero as a sign closes are beating opens.
Look for divergence with price.
Pair it with a trend tool for context.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It reacts quickly and can cross often in ranges.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Schaff Trend Cycle
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Schaff Trend Cycle: a MACD run through two stochastic passes, from 0 to 100, with triggers at 75 and 25.
overview: The Schaff Trend Cycle (STC) is a fast trend oscillator from 0 to 100 in its own pane. Trigger lines sit at 75 and 25.
The line is green while bullish and red while bearish, with a gradient fill from the midline.
how: First a MACD is built from 23 and 50 bar EMAs. Then a stochastic of that MACD is taken over 10 bars and smoothed with a factor of 0.5. A second stochastic pass with the same smoothing gives the final STC.
The two passes make it move quickly between the top and bottom of its range.
use: Some traders watch a cross up through 25 as an early sign of an uptrend.
Watch a cross down through 75 as an early sign of a downtrend.
Use flat lines at the top or bottom as a sign the trend is steady.
Pair it with price structure to filter quick flips.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It can sit pinned at 0 or 100 for long stretches.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: SMI Ergodic Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: SMI Ergodic: double-smoothed price momentum (20 and 5 EMAs) with a 5-bar signal line, or as a histogram.
overview: The SMI Ergodic Indicator shows smoothed momentum in its own pane, with a signal line in orange. In Oscillator display it plots the gap between the two as a histogram instead.
Histogram bars are green when growing and red when falling.
how: Take the one-bar change of the close. Smooth it with a 20-bar EMA, then a 5-bar EMA. Do the same with the absolute change. SMI = 100 x smoothed change / smoothed absolute change.
Signal = 5-bar EMA of SMI. The oscillator = SMI - signal.
use: Some traders watch SMI crossing its signal line.
Use zero-line crosses as changes in momentum direction.
Use the histogram view to see momentum speeding up or slowing.
Look for divergence with price.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is closely related to the True Strength Index.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Stochastic
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Stochastic oscillator: where the close sits in its 14-bar range, smoothed %K and %D, with levels at 80 and 20.
overview: The Stochastic shows where the close sits within the recent high-low range, on a scale of 0 to 100 in its own pane. It has a blue %K line and an orange %D line, with a band between 80 and 20.
With smoothing 3, it is the classic slow stochastic.
how: Raw %K = (close - lowest low of 14 bars) / (highest high - lowest low) x 100. %K = 3-bar SMA of raw %K. %D = 3-bar SMA of %K.
A %K smoothing of 1 gives the fast stochastic.
use: Some traders watch readings above 80 or below 20 as stretched.
Use %K crossing %D as a change in short-term momentum.
Look for divergence between the stochastic and price.
In strong trends it can stay in a zone for a long time.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It moves fast and can cross often in ranges.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Stochastic RSI
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Stochastic RSI: a stochastic of the 14-bar RSI, with smoothed %K and %D lines and levels at 80 and 20.
overview: The Stochastic RSI applies the stochastic formula to RSI instead of price. It moves between 0 and 100 in its own pane, faster than RSI, with a blue %K, an orange %D and a zone between 80 and 20.
It shows where RSI sits in its own recent range.
how: First RSI(close, 14). Then raw = (RSI - lowest RSI of 14 bars) / (highest RSI - lowest RSI) x 100. %K = 3-bar SMA of raw. %D = 3-bar SMA of %K.
Because it measures RSI against itself, it often reaches 0 or 100.
use: Some traders watch moves above 80 or below 20 as short-term extremes.
Use %K crossing %D as a quick momentum signal.
Pair it with a trend filter so you read it in context.
Watch for it leaving an extreme zone.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is very sensitive and gives many signals.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: TradeZoro Market Stats session
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Draws one past session's prior-day levels, open, gap, opening range and initial balance, with a marker where the outcome happened.
overview: TradeZoro Market Stats session is opened from the Market Stats page. It takes you to the chosen date and draws the levels for that one session: prior day high, low and close, the open, the gap band, the opening range (15 or 30 minutes) and the initial balance lines. A marker shows the minute the studied outcome happened.
how: Nothing is fetched by the indicator: the numbers come from the Market Stats page when you open the link. The chart switches to the symbol and timeframe, loads older history until that session is on screen, and zooms to that day.

The stats use a back-adjusted continuous contract, so the levels are shifted by the open basis to line up with the chart's bars. SPX levels are drawn on the ES chart shifted the same way, and the chip says so. The only setting turns the labels on or off.
use: Use it to see how a session from the statistics actually played out on the chart.
Some traders study where the opening range broke compared with the prior day levels.
Use the marker to find the moment the outcome happened and look at the bars around it.
notes: It works from links on the Market Stats page; added on its own it has no session to draw.
The statistics are historical frequencies, not predictions.
On hourly charts the alignment can be about 30 minutes early.

items.name: TRIX
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: TRIX: the one-bar percent change of a triple-smoothed 18-bar EMA, plotted with a 9-bar signal line.
overview: TRIX shows momentum with heavy smoothing, in its own pane around zero, with a signal line in orange.
Colors are green while TRIX is above its signal and red while below.
how: Smooth the close three times with an 18-bar EMA. TRIX = one-bar percent change of that triple EMA. Signal = 9-bar EMA of TRIX.
The triple smoothing filters out small moves. Because it is a percent change, TRIX readings can be compared across symbols.
use: Some traders watch TRIX crossing its signal line.
Use zero-line crosses as trend changes in the smoothed price.
Look for divergence between TRIX and price.
Use it to ignore short noise and focus on larger swings.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It lags because of the triple smoothing.
Its zero line marks where the triple-smoothed average stops rising or falling.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: True Strength Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: True Strength Index: double-smoothed price momentum (25 and 13 EMAs) with a 13-bar signal line.
overview: The True Strength Index (TSI) shows momentum as a smooth line in its own pane, with a signal line in orange.
Colors are green while TSI is above its signal and red while below.
how: Take the one-bar change of the close. Smooth it with a 25-bar EMA, then a 13-bar EMA. Do the same with the absolute change. TSI = 100 x smoothed change / smoothed absolute change.
Signal = 13-bar EMA of TSI. Using the absolute change in the second part keeps the result on a fixed scale.
use: Some traders watch TSI crossing its signal line.
Use zero-line crosses as changes in momentum direction.
Look for divergence with price.
Use high and low readings as signs of stretched momentum for that symbol.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Values usually stay between -100 and +100.
It is closely related to the SMI Ergodic Oscillator.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Ultimate Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Ultimate Oscillator: buying pressure over 7, 14 and 28 bars blended 4:2:1, from 0 to 100, with levels at 70 and 30.
overview: The Ultimate Oscillator, by Larry Williams, mixes three time spans into one line from 0 to 100 in its own pane. Levels sit at 70 and 30.
Using several windows helps reduce the false signals one window can give.
how: Buying pressure (BP) = close - min(low, previous close). True range (TR) = max(high, previous close) - min(low, previous close). For each window, average = sum of BP / sum of TR.
UO = 100 x (4 x avg7 + 2 x avg14 + avg28) / 7.
use: Some traders watch readings above 70 or below 30.
Look for divergence between UO and price, as in the original method.
Use the 50 line to separate up and down pressure.
Compare it with RSI to see how the blend changes signals.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The fast window has the most weight.
Williams' original method also looked for a divergence followed by a break of the oscillator's recent high or low.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Williams %R
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Williams %R: where the close sits in its 14-bar high-low range, from 0 to -100, with levels at -20 and -80.
overview: Williams %R shows where the close sits within the recent range, in its own pane. It runs from 0 (at the high) to -100 (at the low). Levels sit at -20 (overbought) and -80 (oversold).
It is a mirror of the fast stochastic.
how: %R = (highest high of 14 bars - close) / (highest high - lowest low) x -100.
A close at the top of the range gives 0; at the bottom, -100. It uses the high and low of the window, so a single large bar can shift the range.
use: Some traders watch readings above -20 or below -80 as stretched.
Use moves out of those zones as signs of a turn starting.
In strong trends it can stay in a zone; some read that as strength.
Look for divergence with price.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It reacts fast and can be noisy.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Average True Range
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Average True Range: the 14-bar Wilder average of each bar's true range, a plain measure of how much price moves.
overview: The Average True Range (ATR) measures volatility in its own pane. A higher line means bars are moving more; a lower line means quieter trading. It does not show direction.
The line turns orange while ATR is expanding.
how: True range = the largest of: high - low, |high - previous close|, |low - previous close|. ATR = average of true range over 14 bars, smoothed with Wilder's RMA by default.
Other smoothing types can be chosen in the settings.
use: Some traders size stops as a multiple of ATR so they fit current volatility.
Use rising ATR to see when moves are getting larger.
Compare ATR with past readings to see if the market is calm or busy.
Use it to set position size so risk stays similar across symbols.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
ATR is in price units, so values differ across symbols.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Bollinger Bands
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Bollinger Bands: a 20-bar SMA with bands two standard deviations above and below, filled between them.
overview: Bollinger Bands draw a middle line (orange) with an upper and lower band (blue) on the price chart. The bands widen when price swings more and tighten when it is quiet.
The area between the bands is lightly shaded.
how: Basis = SMA(close, 20). Upper = basis + 2 x standard deviation of close over 20 bars. Lower = basis - 2 x the same standard deviation.
Length, source and multiplier can be changed.
use: Some traders watch a tight squeeze of the bands as a sign of low volatility before a larger move.
Use touches of the bands to see price stretched from its average.
In strong trends price can walk along one band; some traders read that as strength.
Use the basis as a mid-line for pullbacks.
