notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
A touch of a band is not a signal on its own.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Bollinger Bands %B
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Bollinger %B: where price sits relative to 20-bar, 2-deviation Bollinger Bands; 1 is the upper band, 0 the lower.
overview: Bollinger %B turns Bollinger Bands into one line in its own pane. A reading of 1 means price is at the upper band, 0 at the lower band, and 0.5 at the middle.
Values above 1 or below 0 mean price is outside the bands. The gradient fill runs from the 0.5 midline.
how: %B = (close - lower band) / (upper band - lower band). The bands use a 20-bar SMA and 2 standard deviations by default.
Overbought and oversold levels default to 1 and 0.
use: Some traders watch readings above 1 or below 0 as price outside its normal range.
Use crosses of 0.5 to see price moving above or below the middle band.
Look for divergence: price makes a new high but %B does not.
Compare it with volume tools to see if moves outside the bands have support.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Bollinger Bands Width
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Bollinger BandWidth: the gap between the bands as a share of the middle line, with squeeze and bulge levels over 125 bars.
overview: Bollinger BandWidth shows how wide the Bollinger Bands are, in its own pane. Low values mean tight bands and quiet price; high values mean wide bands.
It also draws a squeeze level (the lowest width of the last 125 bars) and a bulge level (the highest).
how: BandWidth = (upper band - lower band) / basis. The bands use a 20-bar SMA and 2 standard deviations by default.
When the line reaches the squeeze level it takes the squeeze color; at the bulge level it takes the bulge color.
use: Some traders watch for a squeeze as a sign a quiet period may end with a larger move.
Use the bulge level to see volatility that is unusually high for the window.
Use it with price to choose a direction, since width shows none.
Compare widths over time to see the symbol's normal range.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
A squeeze is a condition, not a direction.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Chaikin Volatility
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Chaikin Volatility: percent change of the 10-bar EMA of high minus low, compared with 10 bars earlier.
overview: Chaikin Volatility shows whether bar ranges are getting wider or narrower, in its own pane around zero. Above zero, the smoothed range is wider than it was 10 bars ago.
The line turns orange during expansion.
how: Smoothed range = EMA(high - low, 10). Chaikin Volatility = (smoothed range - smoothed range 10 bars ago) / smoothed range 10 bars ago x 100.
Both lengths can be changed. It compares two values of the same smoothed range, so the reading shows the speed of change, not the size of the range.
use: Use rising readings to see ranges expanding.
Some traders watch a sharp rise after a quiet stretch as a sign of a new move.
Use falling readings to see the market calming down.
Pair it with a trend tool, since it shows no direction.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It looks only at high-low ranges, not gaps.
Large positive readings are common after sudden moves.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Chandelier Exit
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Chandelier Exit: trailing stop lines set three ATRs from the 22-bar highest high and lowest low.
overview: The Chandelier Exit draws trailing stop levels on the price chart: a long stop below price in green and a short stop above price in red.
It hangs the stop from the recent extreme, like a chandelier from a ceiling.
how: Long stop = highest high of 22 bars - 3 x ATR(22). Short stop = lowest low of 22 bars + 3 x ATR(22).
With Ratchet Stops on, the long stop cannot fall and the short stop cannot rise until the close crosses the stop.
use: Some traders use the long stop as a trailing exit level in an uptrend.
Use a close through a stop as a sign the trend may be changing.
Raise or lower the multiplier to make the stop looser or tighter.
Turn on ratchet mode for stops that only move one way.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It follows volatility, so stops move further away when ATR grows.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Choppiness Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Choppiness Index: how much price wandered versus how far it went over 14 bars, from 0 to 100, with bands at 61.8 and 38.2.
overview: The Choppiness Index shows whether the market is trending or moving sideways, in its own pane. High values mean choppy price; low values mean a cleaner trend.
Bands sit at 61.8 and 38.2 by default, and the line takes the trending or choppy color near them.
how: CHOP = 100 x log10(sum of true range over 14 bars / (highest high - lowest low over 14 bars)) / log10(14).
When price travels far in one direction, the range is large relative to the summed true ranges, so CHOP is low.
use: Some traders avoid trend-following ideas while CHOP is above 61.8.
Use readings below 38.2 to see a strong trend in place.
Watch a drop from high readings as a sign a range may be ending.
Pair it with a direction tool, since CHOP shows none.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Donchian Channels
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Donchian Channels: the highest high and lowest low of the last 20 bars, with a middle line between them.
overview: Donchian Channels draw the upper and lower edge of the recent range on the price chart, with a middle line and light fill.
The upper line is red, the lower line green and the middle gray by default.
how: Upper = highest high of 20 bars. Lower = lowest low of 20 bars. Middle = (upper + lower) / 2.
Only the length can be changed. The lines are flat until a new high or low enters the window or an old one drops out.
use: Some traders watch a close above the upper line or below the lower line as a range breakout.
Use the middle line to see which half of the range price is in.
Use the lower line as a trailing level in an uptrend.
Watch a narrowing channel as a sign of a tight range.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The channel only steps when a new extreme is made or an old one leaves the window.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Historical Volatility
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Historical volatility: the standard deviation of 10-bar log returns, scaled to a yearly figure with 252 periods by default.
overview: Historical Volatility shows how much price has been moving, as a percentage, in its own pane. Higher readings mean bigger day-to-day changes.
By default it is annualized so values can be read as a yearly figure.
how: Log return = ln(close / previous close). HV = standard deviation of log returns over 10 bars x square root of periods per year x 100.
Use 252 for daily bars, 52 for weekly and 12 for monthly. Turn off Annualize to see per-bar volatility.
use: Use it to compare how volatile a symbol is now versus before.
Some traders compare historical volatility with expected volatility from options.
Watch for very low readings, which can come before larger moves.
Use it to adjust position size.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
On intraday charts set Periods Per Year to match the bar count, or turn off annualizing.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Keltner Channels
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Keltner Channels: a 20-bar EMA of the close with bands set two times the 10-bar ATR above and below it.
overview: Keltner Channels draw a middle EMA with an upper and lower band on the price chart. The bands widen with volatility, measured by ATR.
Colors follow direction: bullish and bearish colors with a gray basis.
how: Basis = EMA(close, 20). Upper = basis + 2 x ATR(10). Lower = basis - 2 x ATR(10).
Because it uses ATR, the bands are usually smoother than Bollinger Bands. Length, ATR length, multiplier and source can be changed.
use: Some traders watch closes outside a band as a sign of a strong move.
Use the basis as a level for pullbacks in a trend.
Compare with Bollinger Bands to spot squeezes (as in the TTM Squeeze).
Use the band width to see changes in volatility.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Wider multipliers mean fewer closes outside the bands.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Mass Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Mass Index: a 25-bar sum of the ratio of single to double 9-bar EMAs of the range, with setup 27 and trigger 26.5.
overview: The Mass Index, by Donald Dorsey, watches for range expansion that can come before a reversal. It plots in its own pane with a setup level at 27 and a trigger at 26.5.
The line turns orange once it rises above the setup level and stays that color until it drops below the trigger. This is the reversal bulge.
how: Single = EMA(high - low, 9). Double = EMA(single, 9). Mass Index = sum of (single / double) over 25 bars.
The pattern arms when the line goes above 27 and completes when it falls below 26.5.
use: Some traders watch a completed bulge as a sign the current trend may turn.
Use a direction tool to decide which way the turn could go.
Use the orange color to see when the pattern is armed.
Look at how often bulges happened on past bars of the symbol.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It shows no direction by itself.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Relative Volatility Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Relative Volatility Index: an RSI-style line built from 10-bar standard deviation on up and down closes, levels at 80 and 20.
overview: The Relative Volatility Index (RVI), by Donald Dorsey, looks like RSI but uses volatility instead of price change. It plots from 0 to 100 in its own pane with levels at 80 and 20.
It shows whether volatility has been higher on up bars or on down bars.
how: For each bar, take the 10-bar standard deviation of close. On up closes it goes into the up stream, on down closes into the down stream. Smooth each stream over 14 bars with an EMA (or Wilder RMA).
RVI = 100 x up / (up + down).
use: Some traders use RVI to confirm signals from other tools, as Dorsey intended.
Use readings above 50 as more volatility on up bars.
Watch moves above 80 or below 20 as one-sided volatility.
Compare with RSI to see if volatility agrees with momentum.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Standard Deviation
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Standard deviation of the close over 20 bars, a simple measure of how widely price is spread around its average.
overview: This study plots the standard deviation of price in its own pane. Higher values mean price is spread wider around its average; lower values mean it is tightly packed.
The line turns orange while it is expanding.
how: Standard deviation = square root of the average squared distance of each value from the 20-bar mean.
It is the same measure used to build Bollinger Bands. A larger length gives a slower, smoother line; a shorter one reacts faster.
use: Use it to see when volatility is rising or falling.
Some traders watch for very low readings as a sign of a coming expansion.
Use it to scale stops or bands to current conditions.
Compare it with ATR to see two views of volatility.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Values are in price units, so they differ across symbols.
It treats moves up and down the same way.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: TTM Squeeze
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: TTM Squeeze: momentum histogram with dots that show when Bollinger Bands sit inside Keltner Channels.
overview: The TTM Squeeze, by John Carter, shows two things in its own pane. A histogram shows momentum, and dots on the zero line show whether the market is in a squeeze.
Orange dots mean the squeeze is on; gray dots mean it is off. A cross on the zero line marks the first bar after a squeeze ends (a fire).
how: Squeeze is on when both Bollinger Bands (20 bars, 2 deviations) are inside the Keltner Channels (20 bars, 1.5 ATR).
Momentum is a linear regression of price minus the average of the Donchian midline and the SMA over 20 bars. Bars are solid when building away from zero and dim when fading back.
use: Some traders watch for the first gray dot after a run of orange dots.
Use the histogram color to see momentum direction at the fire.
Watch for momentum fading as a sign a move is slowing.
Use a long squeeze as a sign of building pressure.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Ulcer Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Ulcer Index: the root-mean-square of percent drawdowns from the 14-bar high, with a stress level at 5.
overview: The Ulcer Index measures downside risk in its own pane. It rises when price falls from recent highs and stays down, and it stays near zero in steady uptrends.
A dashed stress line sits at 5 by default, and the line shifts to red as it nears that level. Drawdown columns can be shown too.
how: At each bar, percent drawdown = (close - highest close of 14 bars) / highest close x 100. Square these values, average them over 14 bars and take the square root.
Deeper and longer drops raise the index more than short, shallow ones.
use: Use it to see how painful recent declines have been.
Some traders compare the index across symbols to judge downside risk.
Watch readings above the stress line as deep or long drawdowns.
Use it with trend tools to see if a pullback is getting larger.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It only looks at drops from highs, not upside moves.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Volume
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Volume bars at the bottom of the price chart, green on up candles and red on down candles.
overview: The Volume study draws a bar for each candle along the bottom of the price pane. Bars are green when the candle closed up and red when it closed down.
The tallest visible bar takes 20% of the pane height by default, so volume stays out of the way of price.
how: Each bar is the traded volume of that candle as supplied by the chart's data. The bars are rescaled to the visible range as you scroll or zoom.
Only the colors and the height can be changed.
use: Some traders watch for volume spikes at breakouts or reversals.
Use low volume on pullbacks as a sign of less selling or buying interest.
Compare volume at highs and lows to see where activity was heavier.
Use it with volume tools such as OBV or a volume profile.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Volume differs by data source and market; for some markets it is tick or reported volume.

items.name: Visible Range Volume Profile
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Volume profile for the visible chart: horizontal volume rows by price, with a point of control and a 70% value area.
overview: The Visible Range Volume Profile shows how much volume traded at each price level for the bars on screen. It draws horizontal rows on the side of the price chart; longer rows mean more volume at that price.
Each row is split into up and down volume. The point of control (POC) marks the price with the most volume, and the value area shades the range that holds 70% of it.
how: The visible price range is split into 24 rows by default. Each bar's volume is added to the rows it covers, split by up or down candle. The largest row fills 30% of the panel width.
The value area grows out from the POC until it holds the chosen share of volume. The profile is rebuilt every time you scroll or zoom.
use: Some traders watch the POC as a level price may return to.
Use the value area edges as reference areas for the range.
Use thin rows (low volume) to see prices price moved through quickly.
Zoom to one session to see that session's profile.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Volume is spread across each candle's range, so it is an estimate from bars, not trade-by-trade data.
The profile changes as the visible range changes.

items.name: Session Volume Profile
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Draws a volume profile for each session on the chart, with the point of control and the 70% value area high and low lines.
overview: Session Volume Profile draws one horizontal volume profile per session, starting at the left of each session and covering 40% of its width by default. Each row shows how much volume traded at that price. The point of control (POC), the busiest row, is drawn in orange, and the value area high and low (VAH and VAL) are dashed lines.
how: The profile is built from the chart's candles. Each bar's volume is spread evenly over the rows between its low and high. On futures, rows are 4 ticks by default; on crypto, each session is split into 40 rows.

The value area starts at the POC and grows toward the larger neighbouring row until it holds 70% of the session's volume. For futures you can choose the RTH session (09:30 to 16:00 New York), the overnight session (18:00 to 09:30), both separately, or the full 18:00 to 17:00 trading day. Crypto always uses the UTC day.
use: Some traders watch how price reacts at the POC, VAH and VAL.
Use it to compare where volume built up in today's session with earlier sessions.
Some traders note whether a session opens inside or outside the prior value area.
Use the RTH and overnight split to see how the two sessions differ.
notes: Intraday charts only (1 minute to 4 hours).
It is built from candle volume, so it shows where volume traded by bar range, not trade by trade.
For a profile from recorded trades, see Volume Profile (trades).

items.name: Previous Day POC / VAH / VAL
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Draws the prior session's point of control as a solid line and its value area high and low as dashed lines on today's chart.
overview: Previous Day POC / VAH / VAL draws three price lines from the last full session: the point of control (pPOC) as a solid line, and the value area high and low (pVAH and pVAL) as dashed lines. They use the same definition as the pPOC, pVAH and pVAL on the GEX page.
how: On futures, the indicator takes the prior RTH session (09:30 to 16:00 New York) and builds a volume profile from 5-minute bars, rolling 1-minute bars up to 5 minutes first. Rows are 4 ticks by default. The value area starts at the POC and grows toward the larger neighbour until it holds 70% of the volume.
On crypto, the previous UTC day is used and the row size is chosen from that day's range. The levels are computed from this chart's own bars.
use: Some traders watch how price behaves when it returns to yesterday's POC.
Use pVAH and pVAL to see whether today is trading inside or outside the prior value area.
Some traders mark these levels before the open as reference points.
notes: Needs an intraday chart from 1 minute to 1 hour.
It needs enough history for the previous session; otherwise it shows a short note.
The levels come from candle volume, not individual trades.

items.name: Anchored VWAP (±1/2/3 sd bands)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Plots a volume-weighted average price from a chosen bar, with bands one, two and three standard deviations above and below.
overview: Anchored VWAP draws the volume-weighted average price starting from an anchor bar, with up to three bands above and below it. The area between the first bands is lightly shaded. By default the anchor is the start of the latest session, and you can add more than one copy with different anchors.
how: From the anchor onward, each bar's typical price (high plus low plus close, divided by three) is weighted by its volume. The VWAP is the running sum of price times volume divided by the running sum of volume. The bands are the volume-weighted standard deviation of typical price around the VWAP, at 1, 2 and 3 deviations.
If the chart has no volume, every bar counts equally. You can set the anchor time in the settings, or use the 'click a bar to anchor' row in the picker.
use: Some traders anchor to a major high, low or news bar to see the average price since then.
Use the bands to see how far price has stretched from its average.
Some traders watch how price reacts when it returns to the VWAP line.
Use several copies to compare averages from different starting points.
notes: Built from candles, so it uses the typical price of each bar rather than every trade.
The anchor stays fixed until you change it.

items.name: Volume Weighted Average Price
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: VWAP: the volume weighted average of typical price, reset each session, with optional deviation bands.
overview: The Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) draws one line on the price chart that shows the average price paid, weighted by volume, since the start of the period. It resets each session by default.
The line is green while price closes above it and red while below. Optional bands sit at one, two or three standard deviations, or at percent distances.
how: VWAP = sum of (typical price x volume) / sum of volume, from the start of the anchor period. Typical price = (high + low + close) / 3.

The anchor can be session, week, month, quarter or year (UTC). Bands use the volume-weighted standard deviation of price around VWAP, or a percentage of VWAP. By default only band 1 is shown, and VWAP is hidden on daily and higher charts.
use: Some traders watch whether price holds above or below VWAP during the day.
Use the bands to see price stretched from the day's average.
Watch returns to VWAP after a move as a reference level.
Use a weekly or monthly anchor for a longer view.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Periods reset in UTC.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Relative Volume
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Shows each bar's volume as a multiple of the average volume at the same time of day, as a histogram with high bars highlighted.
overview: Relative Volume (RVOL) draws a histogram in a lower pane. Each bar's value is its volume divided by a normal volume for that bar. A value of 1 means average, marked by a dotted line; bars at or above 2 times average are highlighted in orange by default.
how: On intraday charts the average is the volume at the same time of day over the previous 10 days. If there is not enough same-time history, for example on a short chart, it falls back to a rolling average of the previous 10 bars.
On daily and higher charts it uses a simple average of the previous 10 bars. You can change the lookback and the highlight level.
use: Some traders watch for bars that trade far more volume than usual for that time of day.
Use it to compare the open or a news bar with typical activity.
Some traders check whether a breakout came with above-average volume.
notes: Needs bars with volume.
Same-time averages need several days of intraday history to be meaningful.

items.name: Volume Heatmap
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Shades horizontal bands behind price where the most volume traded in the visible range, coloured by candle direction.
overview: Volume Heatmap paints horizontal rows behind the candles at the prices where volume built up. Busier rows are wider and more opaque. By default each row is green when up candles contributed more of its volume and red when down candles did; a single-colour mode is also available.
how: For the visible bars, each bar's volume is spread evenly across the price rows between its low and high, and added with the sign of the candle (up or down). Rows on futures are 4 ticks by default, and are doubled in size when they would be too thin on screen. On other markets the row size follows the visible price range.
Only rows above 8% of the busiest row are drawn, with opacity up to 42%.
use: Some traders use it to see high-volume price areas at a glance.
Use the colour to see whether up or down candles built each area.
Some traders watch how price behaves when it returns to a heavy band.
notes: Built from candle volume and range, not from trades at each price.
The heatmap follows the visible range, so it changes as you scroll or zoom.
It does not show resting orders; for the order book, see the order-flow heatmaps.

items.name: Auto Chart Patterns
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Finds classic chart patterns from swing pivots and draws them with outline lines, names and a neckline or breakout line.
overview: Auto Chart Patterns looks for classic shapes in price and draws them on the chart. It covers double tops and bottoms, head and shoulders and inverse head and shoulders, ascending, descending and symmetrical triangles, rising and falling wedges, bull and bear flags, and channels.
Each pattern gets outline lines, a small name label and a dotted neckline or breakout line. An optional dotted line shows the measured-move target. By default the newest 6 patterns are shown.
how: The indicator builds a zigzag of swing pivots, with a pivot length of 5 bars each side by default; a larger length finds fewer, larger patterns. Recent pivots are matched against each pattern's shape.

A pattern is shown as forming until a bar closes through its neckline or trendline; then it is complete. Only new closed bars are read, and only the last set of pivots is kept. Each pattern type can be switched on or off.
use: Some traders use it to spot classic shapes they might miss by eye.
Use the forming patterns to see which neckline or trendline price is testing.
Some traders compare the measured-move line with nearby levels.
Use it to practise recognising patterns on past charts.
notes: Patterns depend on the pivot length; different settings find different patterns.
It draws patterns, not signals; many patterns do not play out.

items.name: Anchored VWAP: click a bar to anchor
items.windowName: Anchored VWAP: click a bar to anchor
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Lets you click any candle to start an Anchored VWAP from that bar, with standard-deviation bands, in one step from the picker.
overview: This picker row is a shortcut for Anchored VWAP. After you choose it, the chart asks you to click a bar. The bar you click becomes the anchor, and an Anchored VWAP with its standard-deviation bands is added from that point.
how: The row watches for your next click or tap on the chart and reads the time of the bar under the pointer. It then adds the Anchored VWAP indicator with that time as its anchor. Press Escape to cancel. If no bar was under the pointer, a message asks you to try again.
The line itself is the Anchored VWAP: typical price weighted by volume from the anchor onward, with bands at 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations.
use: Some traders anchor to a swing high or low to see the average price since that turn.
Use it to anchor to a news bar or the session open.
Some traders add several anchors to compare averages from different points.
notes: Each click adds a new Anchored VWAP; you can change its settings afterwards.
See Anchored VWAP for the full description of the line and bands.

items.name: Fixed Range Volume Profile (drag a range)
items.windowName: Fixed Range Volume Profile (drag a range)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Lets you drag across a range of bars to draw a volume profile for exactly that range, using the chart's range drawing tool.
overview: This picker row turns on the fixed range volume profile drawing tool. You drag across the bars you want to study, and a volume profile is drawn for just that range, showing how much volume traded at each price.
how: Choosing the row arms the chart's built-in fixed range volume profile tool and shows a short tip: drag across the bars you want to profile. The profile is drawn as a drawing on the chart, so you can place several and move or delete them like other drawings.
The profile is built from the candles inside the range you select.
use: Some traders profile a single move, such as a rally or a sell-off, to see where volume built up.
Use it to find the busiest price inside a consolidation.
Some traders compare profiles of two ranges side by side.
notes: It is a drawing tool, not an indicator with settings in the indicator list.
It is built from candle volume, not individual trades.

items.name: Accumulation / Distribution
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Accumulation/Distribution line: a running total of volume weighted by where each bar closes in its range.
overview: The Accumulation/Distribution (A/D) line adds up volume, weighted by where each candle closes, in its own pane. It rises when closes sit near highs on good volume and falls when they sit near lows.
With slope coloring on, it is green while rising and red while falling.
how: Money flow multiplier = ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low). Money flow volume = multiplier x volume. A/D = running total of money flow volume.
The level itself has no meaning; the slope and direction are what count.
use: Some traders watch for divergence between A/D and price.
Use a rising line during a range as a sign of accumulation.
Use a falling line during a rally as a sign of weaker support.
Compare it with OBV to see two views of volume flow.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
It ignores gaps between bars.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Chaikin Money Flow
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Chaikin Money Flow: 20-bar money flow volume divided by 20-bar volume, around a zero line.
overview: Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) shows whether money has been flowing in or out over a window, in its own pane. Above zero means more closes near highs on volume; below zero means more near lows.
The line and fill are green above zero and red below.
how: Money flow volume = ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) x volume. CMF = sum of money flow volume over 20 bars / sum of volume over 20 bars.
Values range from -1 to +1. Bars that close near their high add most of their volume; bars that close near the low subtract it.
use: Some traders watch CMF staying above zero as steady buying pressure.
Use zero-line crosses as changes in flow.
Look for divergence between CMF and price.
Use it to check breakouts for volume support.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Bars with no range add nothing.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Chaikin Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Chaikin Oscillator: the 3-bar EMA minus the 10-bar EMA of the Accumulation/Distribution line, around zero.
overview: The Chaikin Oscillator shows the momentum of the Accumulation/Distribution line, in its own pane around zero.
The line and fill are green above zero (accumulation) and red below (distribution).
how: Chaikin Oscillator = EMA(A/D, 3) - EMA(A/D, 10). The A/D line is the running total of volume weighted by where each bar closes in its range.
Both EMA lengths can be changed. Because it uses the A/D line, it reacts to where each bar closes in its range, not only to the close-to-close change.
use: Some traders watch zero-line crosses as changes in buying or selling pressure.
Look for divergence between the oscillator and price.
Use it with a trend filter to read crosses in context.
Compare it with MACD to see momentum from volume rather than price.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
It can move against price when closes sit low in rising bars.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Ease of Movement
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Ease of Movement: how far price moved per unit of volume, smoothed with a 14-bar SMA, around zero.
overview: Ease of Movement (EOM), by Richard Arms, shows how easily price moves, in its own pane. High positive values mean price rose on light volume; large negative values mean it fell easily.
The line is green above zero and red below.
how: Distance moved = (high + low) / 2 - (previous high + previous low) / 2. Box ratio = (volume / 10000) / (high - low). One-bar EMV = distance / box ratio. EOM = SMA(EMV, 14).
The divisor (10000) only scales the line.
use: Some traders watch EOM above zero as price rising with little effort.
Use zero-line crosses as a change in direction of easy movement.
Look at values near zero as heavy volume for little movement.
Pair it with price structure to judge breakouts.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Force Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Force Index: the bar's price change times its volume, smoothed with a 13-bar EMA, around a zero line.
overview: The Force Index, by Alexander Elder, combines price change and volume in its own pane. Above zero buyers had the upper hand; below zero sellers did.
Colors are green above zero and red below.
how: Raw force = (close - previous close) x volume. Force Index = EMA(raw force, 13).
Elder used 13 bars for the intermediate trend and 2 bars for short-term timing. Big moves on big volume give the largest readings.
use: Some traders watch zero-line crosses as changes in who is in control.
Use a 2-bar setting to spot short dips inside a trend.
Look for divergence between Force Index and price.
Watch for spikes as signs of heavy, one-sided bars.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Values depend on the symbol's volume, so they are not comparable across symbols.
A 2-bar length is much noisier than the default.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Intraday Intensity
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Intraday Intensity: volume weighted by where each bar closes in its range, as a 21-bar oscillator or a running line.
overview: Intraday Intensity, by David Bostian, shows whether closes sit near highs or lows on volume. By default it is shown as a normalized oscillator (II%) around zero in its own pane.
You can switch to the cumulative line, which is read by its slope. Positive readings are green and negative ones red.
how: Intensity for one bar = (2 x close - high - low) / (high - low) x volume. II% = sum of intensity over 21 bars / sum of volume over 21 bars x 100.
The cumulative form is the running total of intensity; the length does not affect it.
use: Some traders watch II% staying positive as steady buying near highs.
Use the cumulative line to compare its slope with price.
Look for divergence between the line and price.
Use zero crosses as changes in pressure.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Klinger Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Klinger Oscillator: the 34-bar EMA minus the 55-bar EMA of volume force, with a 13-bar signal line.
overview: The Klinger Oscillator, by Stephen Klinger, compares long-term and short-term volume flow, in its own pane. It has an oscillator line and a signal line in orange.
Colors are green while the oscillator is above its signal and red while below.
how: Trend = +1 when typical price (high + low + close) is higher than the previous bar, -1 when lower. Volume force uses volume, trend and the bar's range. KO = EMA(volume force, 34) - EMA(volume force, 55). Signal = EMA(KO, 13).
Lengths can be changed.
use: Some traders watch KO crossing its signal line.
Use zero-line crosses as long-term flow changes.
Look for divergence between KO and price.
Use it with a trend filter to read crosses in context.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
The volume force also uses a running sum of bar ranges that resets when the trend flips.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Money Flow Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Money Flow Index: a volume-weighted RSI of typical price over 14 bars, with levels at 80 and 20.
overview: The Money Flow Index (MFI) looks like RSI but includes volume. It runs from 0 to 100 in its own pane, with levels at 80 and 20 and a shaded zone between.
It is sometimes called volume-weighted RSI.
how: Typical price = (high + low + close) / 3. Raw money flow = typical price x volume. Over 14 bars, add money flow on bars where typical price rose (positive) and fell (negative). MFI = 100 - 100 / (1 + positive / negative).
Levels can be changed.
use: Some traders watch readings above 80 or below 20 as stretched.
Look for divergence between MFI and price.
Use crosses of 50 as changes in money flow direction.
Compare with RSI to see if volume agrees with price momentum.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Negative Volume Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Negative Volume Index: a running line that moves only on bars with lower volume than the bar before, with a 255-bar EMA.
overview: The Negative Volume Index (NVI) tracks price change only on days when volume falls. The idea is that quieter days show what informed traders are doing. It plots in its own pane with a 255-bar signal EMA.
By default the line is green above its EMA and red below, with a gradient fill.
how: Start at 1000. On a bar with lower volume than the previous one, NVI changes by the same percent as the close. On other bars it stays the same.
The signal is a 255-bar EMA, about one trading year on daily charts. The starting value has no meaning; read the slope and the position against the EMA.
use: Some traders read NVI above its EMA as a sign of a healthy trend.
Use it on daily charts as it was designed.
Compare it with the Positive Volume Index.
Watch the color change when NVI crosses its EMA.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Made for daily charts; the 255-bar EMA needs a long history.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: On Balance Volume
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: On Balance Volume: a running total that adds volume on up closes and subtracts it on down closes.
overview: On Balance Volume (OBV), by Joe Granville, is a running volume line in its own pane. It rises when volume comes on up closes and falls when it comes on down closes.
An optional moving average can be added as a smoothing or signal line.
how: If close is above the previous close, add the bar's volume. If below, subtract it. If equal, OBV stays the same.
The smoothing line can be SMA or another type, 20 bars by default. The level of OBV has no meaning by itself; the slope does.
use: Some traders watch OBV breaking out before price does.
Look for divergence between OBV and price.
Use the smoothing line to see when OBV turns.
Use it to check whether a breakout comes with rising volume.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Percentage Volume Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Percentage Volume Oscillator: the gap between a 12 and 26-bar EMA of volume as a percent, with signal and histogram.
overview: The Percentage Volume Oscillator (PVO) works like a MACD on volume. It shows whether recent volume is above or below its longer average, in its own pane.
It has a signal line in orange and a histogram, with colors for expansion and contraction.
how: PVO = (EMA(volume, 12) - EMA(volume, 26)) / EMA(volume, 26) x 100. Signal = EMA(PVO, 9). Histogram = PVO - Signal.
Because it is a percent, it can be compared across symbols. The signal line and histogram can each be turned off.
use: Some traders watch PVO above zero as a sign of rising activity.
Use it to check if a breakout comes with expanding volume.
Watch PVO crossing its signal line for changes in volume trend.
Use falling PVO in a trend as a sign of waning interest.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Positive Volume Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Positive Volume Index: a running line that moves only on bars with higher volume than the bar before, with a 255-bar EMA.
overview: The Positive Volume Index (PVI) tracks price change only on days when volume rises. It plots in its own pane with a 255-bar signal EMA.
Colors show its position against the EMA, with a gradient fill.
how: Start at 1000. On a bar with higher volume than the previous one, PVI changes by the same percent as the source (close by default). On other bars it stays the same.
The signal is a 255-bar EMA, about one trading year on daily charts. The starting value has no meaning; read the slope and the position against the EMA.
use: Some traders read PVI above its EMA as a sign of a broad uptrend.
Compare it with the Negative Volume Index.
Use it on daily charts as designed.
Watch the color change when PVI crosses its EMA.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Made for daily charts; the 255-bar EMA needs a long history.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Price Volume Trend
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Price Volume Trend: a running total of volume times the percent change in close, with an optional signal line.
overview: Price Volume Trend (PVT) is a running volume line in its own pane, like OBV but scaled by how much price moved.
It is green while rising and red while falling. An optional signal line (21 bars, SMA by default) can be shown.
how: PVT = previous PVT + volume x (close - previous close) / previous close.
Large moves add more volume than small ones, unlike OBV which adds full volume on any up close.
use: Some traders look for divergence between PVT and price.
Use the signal line to see when PVT turns.
Compare it with OBV to see the effect of move size.
Use a rising PVT in a range as a sign of accumulation.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Its starting level has no meaning; read its slope.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Volume Flow Indicator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Volume Flow Indicator: signed volume over 130 bars with a volatility cutoff and volume cap, plus a signal line.
overview: The Volume Flow Indicator (VFI), by Markos Katsanos, shows the balance of buying and selling volume in its own pane around zero. It has a signal line in orange and a gradient fill.
Above zero, volume on up moves has been heavier; below zero, on down moves.
how: For each bar, compare typical price with the previous bar. If the change is larger than a cutoff (0.2 x the 30-bar standard deviation of log changes x close), the volume is added as positive or negative. Each bar's volume is capped at 2.5 times average volume.
VFI = sum over 130 bars / average volume, then smoothed with a 3-bar EMA. Signal = 5-bar EMA.
use: Some traders watch VFI above zero as a sign of net buying volume.
Use zero-line crosses as changes in volume flow.
Look for divergence between VFI and price.
Use it on daily charts as in its original design.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
The 130-bar window makes it slow on purpose.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Volume Oscillator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Volume Oscillator: the percent gap between a 5 and 10-bar EMA of volume, around a zero line.
overview: The Volume Oscillator shows whether short-term volume is above or below a slightly longer average, in its own pane.
It is green above zero and red below.
how: Volume Oscillator = (EMA(volume, 5) - EMA(volume, 10)) / EMA(volume, 10) x 100.
Both lengths can be changed. Because it is a percent, readings can be compared across symbols.
use: Some traders watch a rise above zero during a breakout as a sign of rising interest.
Use falling readings in a trend as a sign of fading activity.
Compare it with price swings to see which moves came on high volume.
Use longer lengths for a smoother view.
Watch for readings that stay below zero in a quiet range as a sign of low interest.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
It shows how active trading is, not whether it is buying or selling.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Session VWAP
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Plots a volume-weighted average price line that restarts at the first bar of each day, using the typical price by default.
overview: Session VWAP is a short example Pine script that draws one yellow line on the price chart: the volume-weighted average price for the current day. The line starts again at the first bar of every new day.
how: On each bar the script adds price times volume to a running sum, and adds volume to a second sum. The line is the first sum divided by the second. Both sums reset to zero when a new day starts.
The price used is the source setting, hlc3 by default (the average of high, low and close).
use: Some traders use VWAP as a reference for the day's average traded price.
Use it to see whether price is trading above or below the day's average.
Some traders watch how price reacts when it returns to VWAP.
Use it as an example of how Pine scripts reset values each day.
notes: It needs volume data; without volume the line is not drawn.
The day boundary follows the chart's daily session.
It has no standard-deviation bands and no alert conditions.

items.name: Aroon
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Aroon Up and Aroon Down: how recently the 14-bar high and low were made, each on a 0 to 100 scale.
overview: Aroon, by Tushar Chande, shows how recently price made a new high or low, in its own pane. Aroon Up is green and Aroon Down is red.
A reading of 100 means the extreme was made on the current bar; 0 means it was made the full length ago.
how: Aroon Up = 100 x (14 - bars since the 14-bar highest high) / 14. Aroon Down = 100 x (14 - bars since the 14-bar lowest low) / 14.
Only the length can be changed.
use: Some traders watch Aroon Up above 70 and Aroon Down below 30 as a sign of an uptrend.
Use crosses of the two lines as changes in trend.
Watch both lines low together as a sign of a range.
Use it to see how fresh the latest high or low is.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Average Directional Index
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: ADX with +DI and -DI: Wilder's directional movement lines and trend strength over 14 bars, key level at 25.
overview: The Average Directional Index (ADX), by Welles Wilder, shows trend strength in its own pane. +DI (green) and -DI (red) show direction, and the ADX line (gray) shows strength.
A dashed key level sits at 25.
how: +DM = high - previous high when that is larger than the down move, else 0. -DM = previous low - low when that is larger, else 0. +DI and -DI = 100 x RMA(DM, 14) / RMA(true range, 14). DX = 100 x |+DI - -DI| / (+DI + -DI). ADX = RMA(DX, 14).
ADX rises in strong trends of either direction.
use: Some traders read ADX above 25 as a trending market.
Use +DI above -DI as a sign buyers lead.
Watch a falling ADX as a sign the trend is weakening.
Use low ADX to switch to range tools.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
ADX shows strength, not direction.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Chande Kroll Stop
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Chande Kroll Stop: long and short stop lines built from ATR offsets of the recent 10-bar highs and lows.
overview: The Chande Kroll Stop draws two stop lines on the price chart: a long stop in green and a short stop in red.
It is a trend-following stop based on volatility.
how: First, preliminary high stop = highest high of 10 bars - 1 x ATR(10), and preliminary low stop = lowest low of 10 bars + 1 x ATR(10).
Then short stop = highest of the preliminary high stops over 9 bars, and long stop = lowest of the preliminary low stops over 9 bars.
use: Some traders watch price above both lines as a sign of an uptrend.
Use the lines as trailing stop levels.
Watch price crossing a line as a possible trend change.
Adjust the multiplier to make stops looser or tighter.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Default settings are P = 10, X = 1 and Q = 9; the short stop sits above price and the long stop below in a steady trend.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Parabolic SAR
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Parabolic SAR: Wilder's stop-and-reverse dots that trail price and speed up as the trend extends.
overview: The Parabolic SAR, by Welles Wilder, plots dots above or below the candles. Dots below price (green) mean an uptrend; dots above price (red) mean a downtrend.
When price crosses the dots, they flip to the other side.
how: SAR next = SAR + AF x (EP - SAR). EP is the extreme point of the trend (highest high in an uptrend, lowest low in a downtrend). AF starts at 0.02, adds 0.02 each time a new extreme is made, and stops at 0.2.
On a flip, SAR resets to the previous extreme point and AF resets to the start.
use: Some traders use the dots as a trailing stop.
Use the flip as a sign of a possible trend change.
Watch the gap between price and dots to see how extended the trend is.
Pair it with a trend strength tool to avoid flips in ranges.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It flips often in sideways markets.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: SuperTrend
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: SuperTrend: a trailing line set three 10-bar ATRs from median price, green in uptrends and red in downtrends.
overview: SuperTrend draws a single trailing line on the price chart. While the trend is up, the line sits below price in green; while it is down, it sits above in red.
The line switches sides when price closes through it.
how: Basic upper band = (high + low) / 2 + 3 x ATR(10). Basic lower band = (high + low) / 2 - 3 x ATR(10). The final lower band can only rise and the upper band can only fall, while the previous close stays on the right side.
The trend turns up when the close goes above the upper band, and down when it goes below the lower band.
use: Some traders use the line as a trailing stop.
Use the color change as a sign of a trend change.
Use a higher factor for fewer flips and a lower factor for more.
Watch the distance from price to see how stretched the trend is.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It can flip often in ranges.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Vortex Indicator
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Vortex Indicator: VI+ and VI- lines from upward and downward vortex movement over 14 bars, compared with true range.
overview: The Vortex Indicator shows two lines in its own pane: VI+ in green and VI- in red, around a baseline of 1.
When VI+ is above VI-, upward movement leads; when VI- is above, downward movement leads.
how: VM+ = |high - previous low|. VM- = |low - previous high|. VI+ = sum of VM+ over 14 bars / sum of true range over 14 bars. VI- = sum of VM- over 14 bars / sum of true range.
Only the length can be changed. Values above 1 mean the vortex movement was larger than the true range over the window.
use: Some traders watch VI+ crossing above VI- as the start of an uptrend.
Use a widening gap as a sign of a strong trend.
Watch the lines tangled near 1 as a range.
Pair it with ADX for strength.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: ZigZag
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: ZigZag: straight lines joining swing highs and lows that reverse by at least 5% with at least 10 bars between pivots.
overview: The ZigZag connects major swing highs and lows with straight lines on the price chart. Rising legs are green and falling legs are red.
Small moves are filtered out so only the main swings remain.
how: A new pivot is confirmed when price reverses from the current leg extreme by at least the deviation (5% of that extreme by default), with at least 10 bars between pivots.
The last leg can change while price is still extending it. Raising the depth spaces pivots further apart; raising the deviation keeps only bigger swings.
use: Use it to see the main swings of a move without noise.
Some traders use the pivots to draw trend lines or measure retracements.
Use it to study the size and length of past swings.
Lower the deviation for smaller swings.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The last leg can move until a new pivot is confirmed.
Lines are drawn after the fact; they mark swings that already happened.

items.name: 52-Week High/Low
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: The rolling 52-week high and low drawn as levels on the chart, with an optional all-time high and low.
overview: This study draws the highest high and lowest low of the last 52 weeks as lines on the price chart. The high is green and the low red.
You can also show the all-time high and low across the loaded history.
how: The window is a rolling span of 52 weeks in time, not a bar count, so it works on any timeframe. The all-time levels track the symbol's full loaded history.
The number of weeks can be changed.
use: Some traders watch the 52-week high as a breakout level.
Use the distance to each level to see where price sits in its yearly range.
Watch reactions near the 52-week low as signs of support.
Use the all-time high to see if price is in new territory.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe.
The all-time levels depend on how much history is loaded.
items.alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.

items.name: Camarilla Pivots
items.author: TradeZoro
items.short: Camarilla levels R5 to S5, Y-High / Y-Close / Y-Low and the R3-RB3 / S3-SB3 zones from the prior day, week or month
items.summary: Draws the Camarilla levels R5 to S5, Y-High, Y-Close and Y-Low from the prior day, week or month, with shaded reversal zones.
overview: Camarilla Pivots draws a ladder of price levels worked out from the previous session's high, low and close. You see R5, R4, RB3, R3, R2 and R1 above, Y-High, Y-Close and Y-Low in the middle, and S1, S2, S3, SB3, S4 and S5 below.

The R/S levels are solid lines, Y-High is dashed green, Y-Low is dashed red and Y-Close is dashed orange. The space between R3 and RB3 is shaded red and the space between S3 and SB3 is shaded green. Each day's levels run from the start of the session to its end, and today's run to the right edge. Name tags sit at the right end and price tags on the price axis.
how: Range is the prior session's high minus its low. R4, R3, R2 and R1 are the prior close plus Range x 1.1 divided by 2, 4, 6 and 12. S1 to S4 mirror them below the close. R5 is high divided by low, times the close, and S5 is the close minus the distance from the close to R5. RB3 and SB3 are the midpoints of R3 and R4, and of S3 and S4.

On futures a session is the exchange day, 18:00 to 17:00 New York time. On stocks, crypto and forex it is the UTC day. Weekly and Monthly use the prior week or month instead. Everything is calculated from the bars on your chart, so the chart needs enough history to hold the previous session.
use: Some traders watch how price reacts when it reaches the shaded R3 to RB3 or S3 to SB3 zones.
Use Y-High, Y-Close and Y-Low to see where price is trading against yesterday's range.
Switch on only the groups you want, such as R3/S3 and R4/S4, to keep the chart clean.
Show a few past days to see how earlier levels lined up with later price.
notes: Made for intraday charts. On a daily or longer chart it shows only the newest set of levels.
You can set the timeframe, the number of past days, colours, line width, labels and price tags.
It marks levels, not signals. Education only. Not financial advice.

settings.title: Shade the R3-RB3 and S3-SB3 zones

items.name: Pivot Points Standard
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Classic pivot points with support and resistance levels from the prior period: Traditional, Fibonacci, Camarilla or Woodie.
overview: Pivot Points draw a central pivot (P) with resistance (R) levels above and support (S) levels below, for each period on the price chart.
The pivot is orange, resistances red and supports green.
how: Traditional: P = (high + low + close) / 3 of the prior period. R1 = 2P - low, S1 = 2P - high, R2 = P + (high - low), S2 = P - (high - low), and so on. Fibonacci adds 38.2%, 61.8% and 100% of the prior range to P. Camarilla scales the range around the prior close. Woodie weights the close more.
Auto timeframe uses daily pivots up to 15-minute bars, weekly on other intraday bars, monthly on daily bars, and yearly above.
use: Some traders watch P as the line between bullish and bearish bias for the period.
Use R and S levels as areas where price may react.
Compare types to see which levels match the symbol's swings.
Use weekly or monthly pivots for a wider view.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Levels are fixed for the period once it starts.

items.name: Previous day high/low
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Tracks each day's high and low and draws the previous day's high in green and low as step lines on the chart.
overview: Previous day high/low is a short example Pine script. It draws the prior day's high and low as flat step lines on the price chart, so you can see yesterday's range while today trades.
how: The script tracks the highest high and lowest low of the current day. When a new day starts, those values become the previous day's high and low, and the tracking starts again. The lines stay flat for the whole day and step to the new values at the next day.
use: Some traders watch how price reacts at the previous day's high or low.
Use it to see whether today is trading inside or outside yesterday's range.
Some traders watch for a break and close beyond either level.
Use it as an example of how Pine scripts carry values from one day to the next.
notes: The day boundary follows the chart's daily session.
There are no settings and no alert conditions.

items.name: Williams Fractal
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Williams Fractals: markers above swing highs and below swing lows that stand out from two bars on each side.
overview: Williams Fractals mark local turning points on the price chart. An up fractal (red, above the bar) marks a swing high; a down fractal (green, below the bar) marks a swing low.
They were made popular by Bill Williams.
how: With Periods = 2, an up fractal is a bar whose high is higher than the two bars before and the two bars after. A down fractal is a bar whose low is lower than the two bars on each side.
A fractal is only confirmed once the later bars have closed, so it appears two bars after the swing. Larger Periods values need more bars on each side, so fewer swings qualify.
use: Some traders use fractals as levels for breakouts.
Use them to place stops beyond the last swing.
Pair them with the Alligator as in Williams' method.
Increase Periods for fewer, larger swings.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Markers appear after a delay of Periods bars.
Many fractals appear in ranges; larger periods reduce them.

items.name: Footprint (bid x ask)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Splits every candle by price and shows the volume sold at the bid and bought at the ask at each price, with imbalances and the POC.
overview: Footprint (bid x ask) opens each candle up into price rows. Each row shows the volume that sold into the bid and the volume that bought at the ask at that price. The busiest price in the bar, its point of control, is boxed, and diagonal imbalances are highlighted.
You can switch the cells to show delta (ask minus bid) or total volume instead. The cells appear when bars are at least 44 pixels wide; zoomed out, the chart falls back to candles.
how: Every trade is tagged by its aggressor: a buyer lifting the ask or a seller hitting the bid. Trades are added up per price row for each bar. Order flow comes from recorded futures trades for NQ, ES, YM, GC, SI and CL (micros use their mini contract's flow) and from public exchange trades for crypto.

An imbalance compares the ask volume at one price with the bid volume one row below (and the bid volume with the ask volume one row above). It is flagged when one side is at least 300% of the other by default. The row size can be set as a multiple of the base step.
use: Some traders look at which side was more aggressive at the high or low of a bar.
Use the boxed POC to see where most of a bar's volume traded.
Some traders watch stacked imbalances as areas where one side dominated.
Use delta mode to see the net buying or selling at each price.
notes: On futures charts use Footprint (L2); a saved futures chart that still holds this one is switched to it automatically. Crypto charts keep this one.
Needs per-trade data; charts without it show a note instead.
In bar replay only data complete at the replay time is used.
Footprint cells need room; zoom in to see the numbers.

items.name: Delta (trades)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Plots each bar's delta, the volume bought at the ask minus the volume sold at the bid, as a histogram in a lower pane.
overview: Delta (trades) draws one histogram bar per candle in its own pane. A bar above zero means more volume bought at the ask than sold at the bid during that candle; below zero means the reverse. Positive bars are green and negative bars red by default.
how: Each recorded trade is tagged by its aggressor side. For every chart bar, the indicator adds up the buy volume and the sell volume and plots buy minus sell. Order flow comes from recorded futures trades for NQ, ES, YM, GC, SI and CL (micros use their mini contract's flow) and from public exchange trades for crypto.
The trades are stored as 1-minute footprint bars and re-aggregated to your chart's timeframe.
use: Some traders compare the size of delta with the size of the candle.
Use it to see whether a push higher came with net buying, or not.
Some traders watch for a large delta that price did not follow.
Use it next to Cumulative Delta to see both the bar and the running total.
notes: On futures charts use Delta (L2); a saved futures chart that still holds this one is switched to it automatically. Crypto charts keep this one.
Needs per-trade data; other symbols show a note.
In bar replay only bars complete at the replay time are used.

items.name: Cumulative Delta (trades)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Plots the running total of buying minus selling from recorded trades as candles or a line in a lower pane, reset each session.
overview: Cumulative Delta (trades), also called CVD, adds each bar's delta to a running total. By default it is drawn as candles in its own pane: each candle's open, high, low and close follow the running total through that bar. You can switch it to a line.
how: Delta is the volume bought at the ask minus the volume sold at the bid, from trades tagged by aggressor side. Order flow comes from recorded futures trades for NQ, ES, YM, GC, SI and CL (micros use their mini contract's flow) and from public exchange trades for crypto.

By default the total resets each session, meaning the futures trading day that starts at 18:00 New York. You can reset by calendar day or not at all. Crypto has no futures session, so it resets on the UTC day and is drawn as a line.
use: Some traders compare the direction of CVD with the direction of price.
Use it to see whether a new high in price came with a new high in CVD.
Some traders watch the CVD slope during a session to see which side is more aggressive.
Use the session reset to compare one day's flow with the next.
notes: On futures charts use Cumulative Delta (L2); a saved futures chart that still holds this one is switched to it automatically. Crypto charts keep this one.
Needs per-trade data; other symbols show a note.
A running total depends on its start point; changing the reset changes the shape.

items.name: Delta
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Draws delta from recorded trades on the price chart in one of 12 styles, from a session delta profile to delta bubbles and a session box.
overview: Delta is an overlay with many looks. The Style setting picks one: H1 session delta profile (the default), H2 split bid/ask profile, H3 volume profile plus delta, H4 visible range against the last 30 minutes, H5 delta profile per time block, H6 delta ladder, V3 delta numbers, V4 delta-coloured candles with absorption, V5 footprint-lite, V6 big delta bubbles, V7 session delta box, and V8 delta heat strip plus CVD.
You can add it more than once, for example H1 and H5 together. Buyers are green and sellers purple by default.
how: Every style is built from the same per-trade order flow as Footprint and Delta (trades): 1-minute bars where each trade is tagged buyer- or seller-initiated. Nothing is estimated from candles. Order flow comes from recorded futures trades for NQ, ES, YM, GC, SI and CL (micros use their mini contract's flow) and from public exchange trades for crypto.

Profiles add up buy and sell volume per price row (auto row size by default) and plot the difference. Block styles group bars into 30-minute or 1-hour blocks. Big delta styles flag bars at 2.5 times the average absolute delta. V7 sums the last 5 minutes into a box in the top right.
use: Some traders use the session profile to see at which prices buyers or sellers were most active.
Use the time-block profile to compare the morning with the afternoon.
Some traders watch the big delta bubbles for bars with unusual one-sided flow.
Use two copies with different styles to see price and bar views together.
notes: On futures charts use Delta (L2); a saved futures chart that still holds this one is switched to it automatically. Crypto charts keep this one.
Needs per-trade data; other symbols show a note.
The pane styles V1 and V2 are in Delta: pane.

settings.title: Style
options: H4 Visible range vs last 30 min
H5 Delta profile per time block

items.name: Delta: pane (bars / CVD + divergence)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Shows delta bars or CVD candles from recorded trades in a lower pane, with strong bars highlighted and price-versus-CVD divergences marked.
overview: Delta: pane has two styles in its own pane. V1 Delta bars draws buying minus selling per bar as a histogram around a dashed zero line, with strong bars highlighted. V2 CVD plus divergence draws cumulative delta as candles and marks divergences with a line on the CVD pane and a dashed line on the price chart.
how: The data is the same per-trade order flow as Footprint and Delta (trades). Order flow comes from recorded futures trades for NQ, ES, YM, GC, SI and CL (micros use their mini contract's flow) and from public exchange trades for crypto.

In V1, a bar counts as strong when its delta is at least 2 times the average absolute delta. In V2, the CVD resets each session by default. A bearish divergence is a higher swing high in price with a lower CVD high between the two pivots; a bullish divergence is the mirror at lows. Up to four of the clearest recent divergences are drawn.
use: Some traders watch for price making a new high while CVD does not.
Use strong delta bars to spot one-sided flow in a bar.
Some traders compare CVD candles with price candles through the session.
notes: On futures charts use Delta (L2); a saved futures chart that still holds this one is switched to it automatically. Crypto charts keep this one.
Needs per-trade data; other symbols show a note.
Divergences are found between swing pivots, so they appear a few bars after the swing.

items.name: Big Trades
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Marks the largest aggressive orders from public crypto exchange trades with bubbles, buyers above and sellers below, with absorption and swept levels.
overview: Big Trades marks only the orders that stand out. Each marker is a buy (green) or sell (red) bubble placed at the order's average price. Bigger and brighter markers mean higher impact. Hover or tap a marker for its details.
When a big order came and price did not follow it, the marker is a hollow ring with an A for absorption. The price range an order swept can also be shown.
how: Consecutive same-side fills within a short burst (150 ms gap, up to 4 ticks of price walk) are joined into one parent order with its total size and average price. items.name: Estimated CVD (from candles)

items.summary: Estimates buying and selling from where each candle closed in its range, and plots it as a cumulative line or per-bar delta.
overview: Estimated CVD (from candles) gives a rough delta for charts with no trade data. It draws a cumulative line in its own pane by default, or per-bar estimated delta as a histogram. A note on the chart says it is estimated from candles, not real order flow.
how: Each candle's volume is split by where it closed in its range. A candle closing at its high counts as all buying, at its low as all selling, and in the middle as even. The formula is volume times (close minus low, minus high minus close), divided by the range.

items.summary: A pane showing the resting bid and ask size near price, their difference, and the change since the session start.
overview: Liquidity Balance (L2) shows how much size rests on the bid and on the ask within a set distance of price, and the difference between them.
Two size lines can be shown, together with the balance.
how: For every order-book snapshot it adds up the resting size within 20 ticks each side of price (by default). The pane shows bid size, ask size, their difference and how the balance has changed since the session began.
use: Use it to see which side of the book holds more size near price.
Some traders watch the balance shift as price approaches a level.
Compare the change since the session start with the session's direction.
notes: Needs the full order book (Data feed L2), which is part of Pro. Works on NQ, ES, YM, RTY, CL and GC futures (micros use their mini's book) and on crypto order books.
Resting size can be pulled at any time.

items.name: Refill Detector (L2)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Marks a price level that was hit by aggressive trades and got its size back within a few seconds.
overview: Refill Detector (L2) puts an R marker on the chart when a resting level is hit by aggressive trades and then refills.
A refilled bid is drawn green and a refilled ask red.
how: A level counts as hit when trades take at least 30 % of its size. It counts as refilled when its size returns to at least 70 % of what it was before the hit, within 3 seconds. All three settings can be changed.
use: Use it to see levels where someone keeps showing size after being hit.
Some traders watch repeated refills at the same price.
Combine it with Absorption to compare refills with price not moving.
notes: Needs the full order book (Data feed L2), which is part of Pro. Works on NQ, ES, YM, RTY, CL and GC futures (micros use their mini's book) and on crypto order books.

It looks at how far from price the resting size is spread, which often changes before or with price speed.
how: For every order-book snapshot it measures how spread the resting size is within 20 ticks of price (by default). Readings at or below the session's 25th percentile are tight; at or above the 75th are wide.
use: Use it to see when the book is thin and spread out or tightly packed.
Some traders compare the regime with the size of the candles that follow.

Use the age to tell new orders from ones that have rested a long time.

overview: Absorption & Iceberg Tracker keeps a running count of three kinds of events in its own pane: absorption, iceberg hints and stop runs.
Buy-side events go up and sell-side events go down, so you can see which side has been showing more of them.
how: Absorption is heavy aggressive volume at a price that price did not move away from. An iceberg hint is a level that keeps refilling as it trades. A stop run is a poke past a recent swing that closes back. Trades come from the trade stream and the book from the order book.
use: Use it to see where the session's absorption and refills have been building.
Some traders compare the tracker with price at highs and lows.

items.name: Wall Events (L2)
items.author: TradeZoro
items.summary: Marks what happens to big order-book walls: eaten, held and refilled, or pulled, right on the heatmap.
overview: Wall Events (L2) puts a marker on each big resting wall when something happens to it. A filled square means the wall was eaten, a hollow square with H means it held or refilled, and a grey x means it was pulled.
It was built because big walls are often filled by many small orders or pulled, which Big Trades (single aggressive bursts) does not show.
how: A wall is either a level that passes the heatmap's colour filter (default) or a level in the top 0.5 % of the session's sizes, and at least 200 contracts or coins. Eaten: at least 50 % of its size traded. Held: at least 50 % traded and price turned away by 4 ticks. Pulled: under 10 % traded while price was within 8 ticks.
use: Use it to see whether big walls get traded, defended or cancelled.
Some traders watch for walls pulled as price comes close.
Use it on top of a DOM heatmap so the markers sit on the bands.
notes: Needs the full order book (Data feed L2), which is part of Pro. Works on NQ, ES, YM, RTY, CL and GC futures (micros use their mini's book) and on crypto order books.
Pulled versus eaten is worked out from trades at the price; it is an estimate.

Hover a bubble for its size.
