items.name: Dynamic Liquidity HeatMap Profile [BigBeluga]
items.author: BigBeluga
items.short: Probable stop-loss liquidity pools above and below price as a heat map plus side histogram, with a peak-liquidity POC.
items.summary: Heat map of likely stop-loss liquidity above and below price, with a side histogram and a highlighted peak-liquidity level.
overview: This community script estimates where stop orders may be resting above recent highs and below recent lows, and paints those areas as horizontal heat lines across the chart. Brighter, thicker lines mark price levels where more estimated liquidity has built up.

To the right of the last candle it draws a profile: one bar per price row, sized by the liquidity collected there, with a percentage label. The row holding the most liquidity is drawn in its own color (orange by default) as a point of control.
how: Over the last few hundred bars (Calculated Bars, 300 by default) the script looks for new short-term highs and lows. At each one it projects a level a little beyond the candle, pushed further out when recent volume is high relative to the window (it uses a 10-bar volume sum and a small ATR step). These levels are stored and removed once price trades through them.

On the last bar the surviving levels are grouped into price rows (Resolution, 50 by default) and their volume is summed per row. Rows above price use the sell liquidity color, rows below use the buy liquidity color, with a gradient from faint to strong.
use: Some traders watch the brightest rows as areas price may be drawn toward to trigger stops.
Use the profile to compare how much estimated liquidity sits above versus below the current price.
Watch the highlighted peak row as the single level with the largest stored liquidity in the window.
Notice when heat lines disappear: it means price has traded through that level.
notes: The liquidity is an estimate built from candle highs, lows, volume and ATR. It does not read the order book.
It needs volume data; on symbols with no volume the levels lose their sizing.
The profile is rebuilt on the last bar, so its shape changes as new bars arrive.
It works on any market and timeframe that has volume.

items.name: 2022 Model Pro+ | ICTKESIK
items.author: ICTKESIK
items.short: Community ICT model script, preserved as supplied
items.summary: ICT 2022-model toolkit: liquidity sweeps, market structure shifts, FVGs, breakers, SMT, key levels, killzones and graded setups.
overview: This community script maps the steps of the ICT 2022 model on the chart. It marks liquidity sweeps with a $$$ tag, the market structure shift (MSS) that follows, the displacement fair value gap, and breaker blocks. It also draws higher-timeframe FVGs, previous day and week highs and lows, session highs and lows, and vertical time lines for midnight, 8:30 and 9:30 New York.
When the steps line up, it draws a setup with entry, stop and two targets, optional risk/reward boxes, a grade, and a checklist table that ticks off each condition.
how: Swings are built from pivots (Swing Length 3 by default). A sweep is a wick beyond a recent swing within a set number of bars; an MSS is a close (or wick) through the opposite pivot within a waiting window. The FVG and breaker come from the displacement leg.

SMT divergence compares the chart with a correlated symbol that it picks automatically for common futures, FX, metals and crypto pairs, or one you choose. Higher-timeframe FVGs come from two timeframes chosen from the chart interval, or set manually.
Each setup gets a grade from how many items it meets (SMT, FVG, premium/discount zone, session). Only setups at or above Min Grade are shown, by default inside killzones only.
use: Use the checklist to see which parts of the model are present on the current setup.
Some traders study the sweep, MSS and FVG sequence to learn how the model is put together.
Watch the higher-timeframe FVGs and previous day levels as reference areas.
Filter by bias or grade to see fewer, stricter setups.
notes: Times and killzones follow New York time.
SMT needs data for the correlated symbol.
Entry, stop and target lines are the script's own rules, not advice; review them on past data before relying on them.
It has many drawings; on small screens you may want to turn some modules off.

overview: This community script is built around the CISD (change in state of delivery) idea. After price sweeps liquidity, it tracks the open of the leg that delivered into that liquidity and prints a CISD line when price closes back through it. Each CISD can carry a grade, a stop level and a strategy checklist.

Around it, the script draws buyside and sellside liquidity lines and sweeps, Asia and London session highs and lows, previous day and week highs and lows, higher-timeframe fair value gaps, and SMT divergence lines.
how: CISDs are found on the chart timeframe and, optionally, on higher timeframes. Max Bars to Confirm (15 by default) limits how long a CISD can take to form. Setups can be filtered by bias and by grade, and invalidated setups can be hidden.

Higher-timeframe FVGs come from up to three timeframes, picked automatically from the chart interval or set manually (60, 240 and D by default). SMT compares swings with a correlated symbol, chosen automatically for common pairs or set by you.
An optional sizing helper shows a contract size from a risk amount you enter.

Some traders combine a CISD with a nearby higher-timeframe FVG or session level for context.

It draws inversion fair value gaps after liquidity sweeps, CISD lines, and the nearest unmitigated higher-timeframe gap on each side. It marks previous week and day highs and lows, Asia and London highs and lows, the all-time high, and the 8:30 AM New York open.

items.name: IFVG° [Pro+]
items.author: Community
items.short: Community IFVG script, preserved as supplied
items.summary: Inverse fair value gap setups after liquidity sweeps, with target lines, invalidation, ghost boxes and a small dashboard.
overview: This community script marks inverse fair value gaps (IFVGs). It watches for a fair value gap that price later closes through, which turns the gap into a zone on the other side. Confirmed IFVGs are drawn as boxes in bullish or bearish colors, with optional midpoint (CE) lines and dotted target lines.
It can also draw sweep lines when swing liquidity is taken, ghost boxes for potential IFVGs, and gray boxes for invalidated setups. A dashboard at the bottom of the chart summarizes the setups.
how: Swings are found on a liquidity timeframe (15 minutes by default) with a swing lookback of 15. By default an IFVG only counts if a liquidity sweep came first, and the inversion must happen within a valid window of 8 bars.

Raw gaps expire after 80 bars if they never invert. A setup is invalidated on a close (or a wick, if set) through the zone. Optional filters limit setups to one or two session windows, to the first and last 10 minutes of each hour, or to gaps that agree with a higher-timeframe FVG.
Up to 15 active setups stay on the chart.
use: Use the boxes to see where a gap has flipped from one side to the other.

items.name: London Intraday Protraction° [Pro+]
items.author: Community
items.short: London/CBDR session ranges, protraction markers, deviations and statistics table
items.summary: CBDR and Asian range boxes, CBDR deviations, London protraction markers and profile labels, with a session statistics table.
overview: This community script follows ICT's London protraction idea for FX. It boxes the Central Bank Dealers Range (CBDR, 14:00 to 20:00 New York) and the Asian Range (20:00 to 00:00), labels their size in pips, and marks each range as valid or invalid against size limits.

It then projects CBDR standard deviations above and below, watches the protraction window (00:00 to 02:00) and the London session (02:00 to 05:00), and marks protraction highs or lows with short level lines and signal text. A statistics table counts how sessions played out, and a panel shows the timeframe and symbol.
how: The ideal CBDR is below 40 pips and the ideal Asian Range between 20 and 30 pips by default; ranges outside these limits are marked invalid. Up to three CBDR deviations can be drawn.

A protraction is confirmed when its extreme holds for a set number of bars (2 by default) and price closes back inside the range. Each day is assigned a profile, such as normal or negated, based on when the protraction printed.
Colors can adapt to a light or dark chart background.
use: Use the range boxes to see whether the day's setup meets the size rules.
Some traders watch the deviation lines as possible areas for the London move to reach.
Use the statistics table to review how often each profile appeared on past sessions.
Compare the protraction marker time with the normal window.
notes: Made for FX pairs; ranges are measured in pips.

overview: This community script looks for manipulation candles: a candle that runs through a key level or a higher-timeframe fair value gap and then closes back. After a confirmation candle it can mark long, short, bulltrap or beartrap setups with stop and target lines.

It also draws session boxes and highs and lows (Asia, London, NY AM, NYSE, London Close, NY PM), daily, weekly and monthly opens, previous day, week and month highs and lows, the midnight open, higher-timeframe FVG zones from up to three timeframes, colored manipulation candles and a dashboard.
how: Signals can come from manipulation candles, almost-manipulation candles, or both, and from key levels, HTF FVGs, or both. The confirmation candle must come within 5 candles by default, and for traps its wick-to-body ratio must be 0.5 or less.

A choppy-market filter asks that the manipulation candle range be at least 0.5 times ATR(14). A higher-timeframe EMA (length 50 on 60-minute data by default) sets the bias: only bullish setups above it, only bearish below.
Stop and target distances scale with the SL and TP multipliers. Only sessions and levels you enable are used.

items.name: Real-Time Big Trades Bubbles & Absorbtions & Deep Pressure
items.windowName: Real-Time Big Trades Bubbles & Absorbtions & Deep Pressure
items.author: samet_lezki
items.short: Big trade bubbles (3 sizes), absorption diamonds and deep-pressure dots.
items.summary: Bubbles on candles with unusual buy or sell pressure in three sizes, plus absorption diamonds and deep-pressure dots.
overview: This community script highlights candles where estimated buying or selling pressure stands out from recent bars. It draws a circle (bubble) inside or beside the candle: green for buying, red for selling, in small, medium or large size depending on how unusual the bar is.
It also marks absorption bars, where pressure was high but the candle body stayed small, and small dots for deep pressure, when net pressure has stayed on one side for a while.
how: The script splits each candle's volume into a buy part and a sell part using where the close sits in the candle range. It then compares each part with its recent average and standard deviation (Lookback 2, threshold 1.5 sigma by default). A bar that clears the threshold, closes in the right part of its range and has a large enough body gets a bubble. Higher scores give bigger bubbles.
Absorption needs the same pressure spike but a small body (at most 0.55 of the range). Deep pressure uses a 10-bar average and a 20-bar EMA of net pressure that both agree in sign.
use: Use the bubbles to see which candles carried unusually heavy one-sided volume.
Some traders watch absorption marks near highs or lows as a sign that pressure is being met.
Use the deep-pressure dots to see which side has been in control over the last few bars.
Turn on the volume filter to keep only bars above average volume.
notes: Buy and sell pressure is estimated from candle shape and volume, not from actual trade-by-trade data.
It needs volume data and works on any market and timeframe that has it.

items.author: Community
items.short: Structure bias, range filter, trend ribbon + 200 EMA, context dots, S/R zones, status panel
items.summary: Structure bias with range filter, 8/21 trend ribbon, 200 EMA, context dots, support and resistance zones and a status panel.
overview: This community script reads market structure and shows a simple state: follow the trend, wait, or stay out of the chop. It draws a fast and slow trend ribbon (8 and 21 by default), a 200 EMA, colored momentum candles and small context dots.

It also marks structure levels with labels, SBS triangles at liquidity rejections, up to three dynamic support and resistance zones, and a status panel with the current phase. An optional table shows the state on four other timeframes.
how: Structure uses two causal swing lengths: a primary (outer) swing of 2 and a local swing of 1. A break is accepted after one close beyond the level. A pullback counts as orderly if it retraces no more than 0.618 of the leg; two local breaks against the primary trend put it on turn watch.

A range is declared after four local flips within 30 bars when the range is no wider than 3.5 ATR; two closes outside end it. Exhaustion dots use RSI(14) above 75 or below 25 and a stretch of 2 ATR from the ribbon. Support and resistance zones come from pivots of strength 15.
use: Use the status panel to see whether structure is aligned, pulling back or turning.

how: The center line has a base length of 40 and adapts its speed using directional efficiency over 14 bars: it reacts faster in clean moves and steadies in noise. Ribbon Spread (0.5) sets the gap between bands.

In Intraday mode an Entry needs at least two counter-trend bars; Scalping mode reacts faster and turns on the phase color engine. After an Entry, price must close beyond the Conf level within 30 bars, or the setup is dropped.

Directional flow is scored from recent bullish and bearish events, including swing breaks. Optional filters can require ribbon direction, ribbon structure, a higher timeframe, or another indicator's value to agree.
